Thalline exciple very thin in upper part, to l00 µm thick in lower part, of intertwined, thick-walled, c. 3 µm thick hyphae with c. 1 µm thick lumina, prosoplectenchymatous in lower part; proper exciple conspicuously enlarged towards the margin, of thick-walled hyphae; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red, C-; hymenium colourless, c. 70 µm high; paraphyses simple or branched in upper part, the terminal cells swollen, (3-)5(-6) µm wide, a few of them with 1-3 broadly ellipsoid 4-6 µm wide terminal cells filled with oil; hypothecium rather thin, with a few oil droplets and hence transparent. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid to subglobose, (9-)10-13(-15) x 5-7.5(-8.5) μm, the septum (3.5-)4-6 µm (1/4-1/2 of spore length). Pycnidia numerous, immersed in 0.2-0.3 mm wide, orange-red warts. Conidia hyaline, ellipsoid to narrowly ellipsoid, 2-3 x 0.7-1.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-, UV+ orange; apothecial disc C-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a temperate species growing on broad-leaved trees, most common in humid areas in the mountains; certainly more widespread in the Alps, but overlooked, or confused with other taxa. The inclusion of this species into Athallia, while the very similar C. flavorubescens is included in Gyalolechia (Arup & al. 2013), may appear quite surprising, but, besides molecular differences, the former has smaller ascospores, shorter and ellipsoid conidia, and lacks fragilin, a substance which is always present in Gyalolechia (Vondrák & al. 2016).

choices.label: Conidia bacilliform. Ascospores (12-)15-18(-19) x 6-10(-11) μm, equatorial thickening 5-9 μm. Paraphyses not of two types. Apex of paraphyses 3-4 μm wide. Thallus yellow-green (to whitish in shade-forms), continuous
Apothecia 0.5-3 mm across. Thalline and proper margins both visible
choices.name: Gyalolechia flavorubescens (Huds.) Søchting, Frödén & Arup var. quercina (Flagey) Nimis
choices.description: Thallus crustose, more or less continuous, sometimes coarsely papillate, yellow-green to yellow-orange in sun-forms, rarely almost grey in shade-forms. Apothecia common, lecanorine, constricted at base, 0.5-3 mm across, with an orange, usually flat disc, an orange prominent, raised proper margin, and a well developed, yellow, often flexuose or crenulate thalline margin. Epithecium brownish orange, K+ red, C+ purple (in section); hymenium colourless, 50-110 μm high; paraphyses c.1.5 µm thick at base, slightly moniliform, with enlarged, up to 4 µm wide apical cells; hypothecium colourless, sometimes inspersed with oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid 12-19 x 6-11 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-8 μm, to half of spore length. Pycnidia rather common, darker orange than thallus, immersed to slightly projecting. Conidia hyaline, bacilliform to slightly pyriform, c. 2 x 0.7 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K+ red, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ red, C+ purple (the latter reaction not always evident). Chemistry: fragilin dominant, with smaller amounts of emodin and parietin; apothecial disc with predominant parietin, and variable amounts of chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a critical taxon, which deserves further study.

choices.label: Apothecia 0.5-1.5 mm across. Proper margin visible, thalline margin not clearly visible
choices.name: Gyalolechia flavorubescens (Huds.) Søchting, Frödén & Arup var. flavorubescens
choices.description: Thallus crustose, more or less continuous, sometimes coarsely papillate, yellow-green to yellow-orange in sun-forms, rarely almost grey in shade-forms. Apothecia common, constricted at base, 0.5-1.5 mm across, with an orange, usually flat disc, an orange proper margin, and a yellow, finally often excluded thalline margin. Epithecium brownish orange, K+ purple-red, C+ purple; hymenium colourless, 50-110 μm high; paraphyses slightly moniliform, c. 1.5 µm thick at base, the apical cells up to 4 µm wide; hypothecium colourless, sometimes inspersed with oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid (10-)11-15(-18) x (5-)6-9(-11) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-8 μm, to half of spore length. Pycnidia common, darker orange than thallus, immersed. Conidia hyaline, bacilliform to slightly pyriform, c. 2 x 0.7 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple (the latter reaction not always evident). Chemistry: fragilin dominant, with smaller amounts of emodin and parietin; apothecial disc with predominant parietin, and variable amounts of chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a mainly temperate lichen, most common on old, more or less isolated deciduous trees, especially oaks; a member of a difficult and variable group.

choices.label: Mature ascospores 4-celled
choices.name: Xanthocarpia ochracea (Schaer.) A. Massal. & De Not.
choices.description: Thallus crustose, endosubstratic to thinly episubstratic, well-delimited, smooth and continuous to minutely cracked, the surface ecorticate, forming large irregular patches sometimes delimited by a dark line, the thallus colour varying according to light exposure, from almost white in shade-forms to orange in sun-forms, usually ochraceous yellow. Apothecia frequent, 0.2-0.6(-0.8) mm across, at first urceolate and immersed, then sessile, with a flat to slightly convex, orange to dark orange disc and a usually paler, mostly yellow-orange, persistent proper margin. Proper exciple orange-brown in outer part, colourless within, the pigmented part K+ purple-red: epithecium orange, with granular crystals, K+ purple-red; hymenium usually colourless, amyloid; paraphyses simple or branched in upper part, 1-2 μm thick at mid-level, the apical cells 2-5 μm wide; hypothecium colourless, usually not amyloid. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores apparently 3-septate at maturity, the lumina dumbbell-shaped, the loculi connected by a wide canal, hyaline, ellipsoid, 11-19 x 5-9 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: apothecia and pigmented parts of thallus K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). White thalli of shaded sites react K-. Note: a warm-temperate species found on hard, compact limestones in sheltered situations, with optimum in the submediterranean belt; in Southern Italy it occurs in the beech belt as well, and in the Mediterranean belt it is confined to more humid-shaded situations, such as within deciduous open forests. For further details see Hafellner & Poelt (1979).

choices.label: Mature ascospores 2-celled
Mature ascospores strongly swollen at septum and thickened at apex, with reduced lumina, recalling the Mischoblastia- type spores of some Rinodina-species
Ascospores different
Thallus episubstratic, thick, distinctly areolate. Apothecia 0.35-0.7(-1) mm across
choices.name: Variospora glomerata (Arup) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, yellow-orange, epruinose, consisting of adjacent, usually flat or slightly convex, angular to irregular, 0.2-1 mm wide areoles, forming 1-3 cm wide patches, without a distinct prothallus. Apothecia usually abundant and characteristically crowded, zeorine, immersed in the areoles to finally subsessile, round to irregular in outline, 0.35-0.7(-1) mm across, with a reddish-orange, flat to slightly convex, epruinose disc and a slightly paler, smooth, persistent but finally very thin margin. Thalline exciple, when developed, c. 50 µm wide; proper exciple 50-100 µm wide; epithecium orange, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, (60-)70-90 μm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched, 1-2.5 μm thick at mid-level, the apical cells up to 4(-5) μm wide; hypothecium colourless, with up to 7 µm large oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid to slightly rhomboid, with apically thickened walls, often swollen in the middle, (12-)14-18.5(-20) x (6-)7.5-11.5(-13) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-5 μm, the lumina concave, more or less heart-shaped, recalling the Mischoblastia- type spores of some Rinodina-species. Pycnidia orange, immersed. Conidia bacilliform. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a mainly Mediterranean species with an areolate, usually richly fertile thallus bearing several crowded apothecia per areole, and ascospores with lumina recalling the Mischoblastia-type, found on limestone in Circinaria calcarea communities; probably more widespread in Southern Italy, but overlooked, or confused with other species. For further details see Navarro-Rosinés & Hladun (1992).

choices.label: Thallus thin endo- or hemiendosubstratic. Apothecia 0.25-0.4(-0.5) mm across
choices.name: Variospora latzelii (Servít) S.Y. Kondr.
choices.description: Thallus crustose, thinly episubstratic or hemiendosubstratic, pale yellow to orange, forming up to 2 cm wide patches. Apothecia zeorine, 0.25-0.4(-0.5) mm across, sessile, with a concave to finally flat, epruinose, orange-red disc and paler proper margin. Proper exciple 40-90 μm wide, prosoplectenchymatous, of radially arranged hyphae, orange in outer part, colourless within; epithecium orange-brown, with granules of anthraquinones reacting K+ purple-red, 10-15 μm high; hymenium colourless 90-100 μm high; paraphyses simple or forked in upper part, 1.5-2 μm thick at mid-level, not moniliform, the apical cells up to 4 μm wide; hypothecium colourless, 70-120 μm high. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, 12-13(-18) x 7-11 μm, at maturity strongly swollen at septum and thickened at apex, with reduced lumina, recalling the Mischoblastia- type spores of some Rinodina-species. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a calcicolous species avoiding direct sunlight, often occurring together with the superficially similar Xanthocarpia ochracea, with an apparently eastern distribution in Europe, known from the Balkan Peninsula (Dalmatia to Greece), and from eastern Asia (Turkey, Russian Caucasus, Israel). The species was synonymised with Variospora dalmatica by Poelt (1969), but that species has quite different ascospores; according to Navarro-Rosinés & Hladun (1992) it could be that material distributed by Massalongo is heterogeneous. To be looked for in southern Italy.

choices.label: Equatorial thickening of ascospores ("septum") not exceeding 1/5 of spore length, usually up to 3 μm
Equatorial thickening exceeding 1/5 of spore length, usually >3 μm
Lichenicolous on Clauzadea immersa
choices.name: Caloplaca nubigena (Kremp.) Dalla Torre & Sarnth.
choices.description: Thallus crustose, endosubstratic or very thinly episubstratic, ochraceous orange to orange, continuous in endolithic forms to granular-rimose in epilithic forms, forming well-delimited, more or less orbicular patches, sometimes delimited by a thin pale prothallus, developing on the thalli of Clauzadea immersa. Apothecia pseudolecanorine, 0.2-0.5(-1) mm across, at least at the beginning immersed in pits of the rocks or (in epilithic forms) immersed in the thallus, later subsessile, with a dark orange, usually flat disc, and a slightly paler, often finally excluded proper margin, without a thalline margin. Proper exciple paraplectenchymatous, c. 140 µm wide, with a few algae at the base; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 70-100 µm high; paraphyses mostly simple, with swollen, up to 7 µm wide apical cells; hypothecium colourless, rather indistinct, prosoplectenchymatous. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 9-13(-15) x (3-)5-7 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2.5-4(-5) µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with unidentified anthraquinones. Note: on calcareous rocks in upland areas, often near summits. Similar to C. coccinea, but differing in morphology, thallus colour, altitudinal distribution (not restricted to above treeline) and in its parasitism on Clauzadea immersa. See also note on C. keissleri. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: Not on Clauzadea immersa
Apothecia scarlet red, immersed in the rock at least when young
choices.name: Caloplaca coccinea (Müll. Arg.) Poelt
choices.description: Thallus crustose, indistinct and endosubstratic, or episubstratic and consisting of very small, scattered, orange-pink areoles often visible only around the apothecia. Apothecia biatorine or zeorine, 0.2-0.8(-1) mm across, at first immersed, then sessile and slightly projecting, with a flat to weakly convex, deep carmine red, smooth disc, and an initially prominent, then thinner, slightly paler, smooth proper margin. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, 60-100 μm wide, with very few to no algal cells; epithecium orange, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 50-70 mm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched in upper part, 1.5-2 µm thick at mid-level, the terminal cells swollen, to 5(-7) μm wide; hypothecium colourless, prosoplectenchymatous, usually inspersed with oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 8-12(-13.5) x (3-)5-7.5 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2-5 μm. Pycnidia usually abundant, partially immersed, the ostiolar region orange-red. Conidia bacilliform, 2.5-3.5 x 1.5 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with emodin, fallacinal, parietin, parietinic acid, and teloschistin. Note: on steeply inclined, partially shaded surfaces of calcareous rocks above treeline; known from the mountains of southern Europe, and certainly ranging throughout the Alps. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: Apothecia yellow to rust-orange, not immersed in the rock
Lichenicolous on cyanolichens (usually Spilonema)
choices.name: Pachypeltis castellana (Räsänen) Søchting, Frödén & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, brownish orange, usually associated with cyanobacterial lichens, consisting of dispersed to crowded, flat to convex,sometimes weakly lobulate dull, epruinose, up to 1 mm wide areoles, without a distinct prothallus. Thallus paraplectenchymatous throughout; medulla I+ blue at least in basal parts. Apothecia zeorine, yellow-orange, dispersed or grouped, round, 0.3-1(-3) mm across, at first adnate then sessile and constricted at base, with a flat to slightly convex disc, a paler, thick, waxy, shining thalline margin, and often a thin, reddish orange parathecial ring; the apothecial margin is sometimes partly blue-grey to greenish due to the presence of the Cinereorufa-green pigment, which reacts K-, N+ purple. Thalline exciple corticate, c. 20 μm thick; proper exciple laterally expanded; epithecium brownish yellow, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 65-70 µm high; paraphyses free, slender, sometimes submoniliform in upper part, the apical cells 4-5 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, narrowly clavate, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (9-)10-13(-15) x (3.5-)5-7(-8) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) rather short, 2-3.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997); apothecia and parts of thallus sometimes with the Cinereorufa-green pigment. Note: on steep rock faces of mineral-rich schists with variable contents of calcium, often growing on cyanobacterial lichens (Spilonema); widespread in the Holarctic region, with scattered records from the Alps, outside the Italian territory: to be looked for in the Italian Alps.

choices.label: Not on cyanolichens
Most ascospores >14 μm long
Most ascospores < 14 μm long
Mature ascospores spindle-shaped, pointed at both ends
choices.name: Variospora paulii (Poelt) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, consisting of scattered to crowded, yellow-orange, epruinose areoles developing on a thin prothallus, forming irregular to more rarely orbicular rosettes, the central ereoles 0.5-1.5 mm wide, round to lobulate, usually strongly convex and sometimes substipitate, the marginal ones most often larger and shortly radiating, 1-2 mm long, 0.5-1 mm wide. Apothecia zeorine, often crowded, up to 1(-1.5) mm across, with a brownish orange, flat to slightly convex disc, a thalline margine concolourous with thallus, and a thin more brownish orange, finally sometimes almost excluded proper margin. Thalline exciple developed only on the lower side of the apothecial margin, rich in algae in lower part; proper exciple rather thick, merging with the hypothecium; epithecium orange-brown, with a fine epipsamma reacting K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 50-70 µm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched, the apical cells swollen, 5-6 µm wide: hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, indistinctly polarilocular, hyaline, long-ellipsoid to spindle-shaped, often with pointed ends and slightly constricted in the middle at maturity, (12.5-)14-18.5 x 5-7.5(-8) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 1-2(-3) µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: on weakly to steeply inclined surfaces of limestone and marl slates in upland areas; known from various Eurasian orobiomes and from Greenland, and from many localities in the Alps, but rather rare or poorly collected.

choices.label: Mature ascospores with rounded ends
Thallus of granules or small areoles, most evident in apothecial surroundings
choices.name: Xanthocarpia crenulatella (Nyl.) Frödén, Arup & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose, usually episubstratic but sometimes poorly evident, yellow to yellow-orange, areolate or of scattered granules, usually developed only near the apothecia, Cortex thin, indistinct, with yellowish orange crystals; algal layer continuous, Apothecia zeorine, frequent, sessile, (0.4-)0.5-0.7(-1) mm across, often crowded, with an orange to brown-orange disc, a slightly paler orange proper margin and sometimes a poorly developed, warted thalline margin which tends to disappear in older apothecia. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, orange-brown in outer part, colourless within, (50-)80-100 μm thick, the pigmented part K+ purple-red; epithecium with numerous yellow-brown crystals, K+ purple-red, C-; hymenium colourless, 85–100(–120) μm high; paraphyses simple to sparingly branched and moniliform in upper part, the apical up to 4-6 μm wide; hypothecium colourless, sometimes with a few oil droplets, prosoplectenchymatous. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, narrowly ellipsoid, (13-)15-20(-22) x (4.5-)6-9(-10) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 1-3 μm (<1/8 of spore length). Photobiont: chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a mild-temperate to subtropical species, often found on calcareous walls, perhaps parasitic of Verrucaria nigrescens when young, very much misunderstood in the past (see note on X. lactea). Recently, this taxon has been considered to be complex and to contain at least four lineages (Vondrák & al. 2011). Very similar is Caloplaca bisagnonis B. de Lesd., described from Liguria, which, according to Roux & Coll. (2025), differs in the smaller spores measuring 11-15(-17) x 4-7.5 μm, and the longer septum (2-4 μm). Several records from siliceous rocks, such as those of Nimis & Tretiach (1999) from Abruzzo and Basilicata, refer to X. diffusa.

choices.label: Thallus areolate, effuse, not restricted to apothecial surroundings
Ascospores (11-)14-16.5(-17.5) x (5-)6-8(-9) µm. Thallus diffuse at margin, often with a distinct grey-white prothallus. On siliceous maritime rocks or on freshwater shores
choices.name: Xanthocarpia diffusa (Vondrák & Llimona) Frödén, Arup & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, areolate, yellow, ochre-yellow or grey-yellow, forming patches to several cm in diam., the marginal parts diffuse, often delimited by a pale prothalline line, the areoles angular, 0.17-0.7(-1.1) mm wide, to 150 µm thick. True cortex absent, but an up to 20 µm thick alveolate cortex (sensu Vondrák & al. 2009) sometimes present; medulla poorly evident. Apothecia zeorine, 0.4-0.7(-1) mm across, with a pale to dark orange disc and an often crenulate thalline margin. Thalline exciple (60-)80-125(-150) µm thick; proper exciple with yellow-orange granules, (30-)40-120(-150) µm thick, the upper part of isodiametrical, 5-7 µm wide cells, the lower part prosoplectenchymatous; epithecium organge, K+ purple-red, C-; hymenium colourless, 70-90 µm high; paraphyses branched, the apical cells 3.5-5.7 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, (11-)14-16.5(-17.5) x (5-)6-8(-9) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2-3.5 µm. Pycnidia indistinct or forming orange spots. Conidia narrowly ellipsoid to short-bacilliform, 2.7-3.2 x 1-1.7 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-, UV+ orange. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: on base-rich siliceous rocks. According to Roux & coll. (2014) the type of Caloplaca prinii B. de Lesd. belongs to this species: the latter name having priority a new combination would be required if the synonymy will be confirmed by molecular data. See also note on X. crenulatella.

choices.label: Ascospores 14.5-20(-23) x 5-7(-8) µm. Thallus sharply delimited by marginal areoles, without a clear prothallus. On calcareous inland rocks
choices.name: Xanthocarpia interfulgens (Nyl.) Frödén, Arup & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, yellow to yellow-orange, areolate-subsquamulose, without a distinct prothallus, the areoles of very different sizes and shapes, from granulose to subsquamulose, (0.3-)1-3(-4) mm wide, dispersed or contiguous, the smaller ones usually convex, otherwise flat or with an irregular-wrinkled surface, the peripheral ones sometimes slightly elongate and/or lobulate at margin. Apothecia zeorine, sessile, 0.3-0.5(-0.6) mm across, with an orange, concave to flat disc and a smooth to crenulate, persistent proper margin. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, 120-150 µm wide; epithecium brownish yellow, 10-15(-20) µm high, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 90-120 µm high; paraphyses simple or forked in upper part, 1.5-2 µm thick at mid-level, the apical cells 3-5 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci (4-)6-8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 14.5-20(-23) x 5-7(-8) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 1-3(-4) µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a species ranging from Central Asia to the Mediterranean Region, found on sun-exposed calcareous, more rarely basic siliceous rocks wetted by rain in at least seasonally dry habitats. Most records from southern Europe, including those from Italy, need to be checked.

choices.label: Thallus thick, forming compact patches to 5 mm in diam. Apothecia immersed in the thallus. Rare species of siliceous substrata
choices.name: Caloplaca sarda Poelt & Nimis
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, pale orange, rimose-areolate, rather thick, forming small, compact, sometimes confluent, up to 5 mm wide patches. Areoles flat, angular, 0.2-0.5 mm in diam. Thallus subparaplectenchymatous throughout, with angular, thick-walled cells; in the algal-free lower medulla they measure 3-6 μm, in the cortex they are horizontally elongate and may reach up to 8 μm. Apothecia orange, one to two per areole, completely immersed in the areoles or weakly emerging, in which case a thin proper margin is evident, otherwise immarginate, with a flat disc. Proper exciple radially expanded at margin, subparaplectenchymatous, with strongly conglutinated-swollen hyphae; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, c. 50 μm high: paraphyses strongly conglutinated, 2-2.5 μm thick at base, the apical cells only slightly thicker, and (in water) difficult to distinguish, becoming free in K. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, mostly poorly developed or only partially ripe, broadly ellipsoid, c. 11-12 x 6.5-8.5 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2.5-3 μm at maturity. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with unidentified anthraquinones. Note: a very peculiar species, hitherto known only from the type locality, on basic siliceous rocks in a dry internal valley of central Sardinia. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: Thallus thin. Apothecia not immersed in the thallus. On calcareous substrata
Thallus well-evident, continuous to rimose. Apothecia rust-orange to orange-brown. Most frequent below treeline
choices.name: Caloplaca adriatica (Zahlbr.) Servít
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, well-delimited, bright yellow, rather thin, usually rimose-areolate. Apothecia 0.2-0.8(-1) mm across, at first immersed, then sessile, with a flat, rust-orange to orange-brown disc and a rather thick, paler orange proper margin which tends to disappear in mature apothecia. Proper exciple orange in outer part, colourless within, the pigmented part K+ purple-red; epithecium with yellow-brown crystals, K+ purple-red; hymenium and hypothecium colourless; paraphyses usually unbranched, enlarged at apex. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 9-13 x 3-4(-6.5) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 1-2.5(-3) µm, c. 1/2 of spore length. Photobiont: chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with unidentified anthraquinones. Note: a Mediterranean to mild-temperate lichen found on steeply inclined surfaces of hard limestone rocks. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: Thallus reduced to a few yellow to orange granules. Apothecia orange. Most frequent above treeline
Ascospores ellipsoid to broadly ellipsoid, 10-13 x 6-10 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) up to 4 μm
choices.name: Variospora macrocarpa (Anzi) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, yellow-orange to orange, consisting of more or less dispersed areoles-granules which are mostly hidden by the apothecia, sometimes poorly developed and inapparent. Apothecia usually abundant, zeorine, sessile, c. 1 mm across, with a flat to slightly convex, orange-red disc and a paler, persistent margin. Epithecium orange, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched, c. 2 μm thick at mid-level, with slightly swollen apical cells; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid to broadly ellipsoid, 10-13 x 6-10 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) up to 3(-4) μm long, <1/4 of spore length. Pycnidia orange, immersed. Conidia bacilliform. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: this poorly known species growing on calcareous rocks, with optimum above the montane belt, appears to be common in the Austrian Alps and should be looked for more intensively in Italy. According to Vondrák (in litt.), however, most of the material called Caloplaca macrocarpa by Poelt and Hafellner (GZU) belongs to Athallia brachyspora (Mereschk.) Halıcı & Vondrák, which is locally common on base-rich siliceous and limestone rocks in the European mountains (see Palice & al. 2018).

choices.label: Ascospores narrowly ellipsoid, 7-11(-13) x 3-4.5 µm, the equatorial thickening 1-2 μm
choices.name: Caloplaca cacuminum Poelt
choices.description: Thallus crustose, at first perhaps facultatively parasitic, but soon becoming autotrophic, ochraceous yellow to yellow-orange, finely areolate or consisting of a few dispersed granules, when well-developed forming small, up to 2 cm wide patches. Areoles indistinct or rounded-angular, separated by deep cracks, flat to slightly convex, 0.2-0.5 mm wide, subparaplectenchymatous throughout, filled by algae which almost reach the upper surface. Apothecia zeorine, usually 1 per areole, broadly adnate to slightly constricted at base, 0.2-0.8 mm across, with a flat to slightly convex, orange disc, and a paler, yellow-orange, persistent margin. Exciple of slightly radiating hyphae, I-; epithecium orange-brown, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 60-80 µm high, I+ blue; paraphyses mostly simple, 1.5-2 µm thick at base, the apical cells up to 6.5 µm wide, covered in a granulose epipsamma; hypothecium colourless, I-. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, narrowly ellipsoid to spindle-shaped, 7-11(-13) x 3-4.5 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) often poorly developed, 1(-2) µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with unidentified anthraquinones. Note: a probably arctic-alpine species typical of Alpine peaks, found on limestone and dolomite in exposed habitats, often starting the life-cycle on other lichens; probably widespread throughout the Alps. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.; according to Vondrák (in litt.) the few available sequences suggest that it could be a limestone variant of the silicicolous, arctic-alpine Amundsenia approximata (Lynge) Søchting, Arup & Frödén.

choices.label: Thallus not lichenicolous
Thallus lichenicolous at least in the early stages of development (look for young thalli!)
On calcareous substrata
On siliceous substrata
Apothecia rusty red, dark orange-brown or dark orange-red, the colour strongly contrasting with that of the thallus
Apothecia yellow to orange
On limestone, exclusively Mediterranean and mostly more or less coastal, rare
choices.name: Gyalolechia luteococcinea (Cl. Roux) Cl. Roux, M. Bertrand & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, finely rimose-areolate, bright yellow to yellow-orange, often delimited by a thin, blue-black prothalline line. Apothecia biatorine, at first immersed, then sessile, rounded, 0.2-1.3 mm across, with a rusty red to dark orange-red, at first flat, then convex, epruinose disc, and a somewhat paler, smooth, at first well-visible, finally often excluded proper margin. Epithecium brownish orange, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 40-60(-80) µm high; paraphyses simple or forked in upper part, not anastomosing, c. 1 µm thick at base, the apical cells (2-)3-4.5 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (9-)10-13(-14) x (3-)5-6(-10) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) up to 5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K+ purple-red; C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ red. Chemistry: thallus with fragilin; apothecia with parietin and emodin (major), and citreorosein, emodinal, fallacinal and parietinic acid (minor). Note: a Mediterranean lichen found on more or less sheltered calcareous rocks, usually not far from the coast but not strictly maritime.

choices.label: On calciferous siliceous rocks, from the Mediterranean to the montane belt, common
choices.name: Gyalolechia flavovirescens (Wulfen) Søchting, Frödén & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, almost continuous to rimose-areolate, up to 0.5 mm thick, well-delimited, sometimes with a black prothallus when young, pale dirty yellow to dirty yellowish orange, sometimes with a greenish tinge. Cortex cellular, 15-22(-30) µm thick; algal layer continuous; medulla white, paraplectenchymatous Apothecia zeorine, adnate, 0.4-1.3 mm across, with a dark orange to brownish red (paler in young apothecia), flat to convex, epruinose disc, a persistent to usually disappearing thalline margin concolorous with thallus and a proper margin which is usually slightly paler than disc. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, of radiating hyphae; epithecium golden yellow, granular, K+ purple-red, C- or C+ purple; hymenium colourless, 70-100(-120) µm high, not inspersed; paraphyses unbranched or sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells slightly swollen, up to 3.5 µm wide; hypothecium colourless, not inspersed with oil droplets, prosoplectenchymatous. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (10-)12-18(-20.5) x (5.5-)7-9(-12) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (3.5-)4-8(-10) µm (1/2-1/3 of spore length). Pycnidia totally immersed, the ostiolar region orange. Conidia bacilliform, 2.5–5 x 1–1.5 μm, Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia C+ purple (reaction often poorly evident). Chemistry: thallus with fragilin (major), emodin, parietin and other anthraquinones (minor); apothecia with predominant parietin and variable, usually low amounts of chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a mainly temperate species with optimum on weakly calcareous sandstone and calciferous schists, on boulders and walls, with optimum at relatively low elevations.

choices.label: Ascospore wall distinctly thickened at apex
choices.name: Flavoplaca calcitrapa (Nav.-Ros., Gaya & Cl. Roux) Arup, Frödén & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose, endosubstratic to usually episubstratic, irregularly areolate, yellow to rarely yellow-orange, forming 5-15 mm wide, irregular patches, the areoles 0.3-0.9 mm wide, flat to almost bullate, scattered to contiguous, esorediate. Apothecia zeorine, 0.3-0.8(-1.5) mm across, sessile, constricted at base, round or irregular in outline, with a flat to convex, yellow-orange disc, a concolorous, thick, thalline margin, and a more or less evident parathecial ring. Thalline exciple rich in algal cells usually confined to the basal part; proper exciple of radiating hyphae; epithecium orange, 8-15 μm high, granulose, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 45-90 µm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched, 1.5-3 µm thick at base, the apical cells up to 3-6(-7) µm wide; hypothecium colourless, inspersed with oil droplets. Asci (6-)8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid, (7-)9-14(-17) x (4.5-)6-7.5(-9) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-6.5 µm, the lumina sometimes sandglass-shaped. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a recently-described species, resembling Athallia inconnexa, but non-parasitic and with different spores and ecology, found on horizontal or weakly inclined surfaces of compact calciferous rocks, especially in fissures; perhaps more widespread in Mediterranean Italy. The sample from Marche was collected at Ancona, on coastal rocks.

choices.label: Ascospore wall not thickened at apex
Coastal-maritime species
choices.name: Flavoplaca maritima (B. de Lesd.) Arup, Frödén & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, ochraceous yellow to pale orange, rimose-areolate, the areoles convex, uneven and knobby, forming orbicular to irregular, extensive patches delimited by an orange prothallus, the margins not lobulate (areoles becoming smaller towards the thallus margin). Cortex paraplectenchymatous, K+ purple-red. Apothecia zeorine, yellow-orange, often clustered, sessile when young but soon raised and constricted at base, 0.5- 0.8(-1) mm across, with a flat slightly convex, orange disc, a slightly raised, smooth, often paler proper margin and a sometimes finally excluded thalline margin. proper exciple of radiating, thick-walled, tightly packed hyphae; epithecium orange-brown, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless; paraphyses somewhat moniliform, simple to branched, 1-2(-3.5) μm thick at mid-level, the apical cells swollen; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 10-16 x 5-8 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3.5-5.5 µm (c. 1/3 of spore length). Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a maritime-coastal species, often confused with F. marina, growing both on siliceous and calcareous rocks, known from the Atlantic coasts and also reported from Corsica (Roux & Coll. 2025). To be looked for in Italy, especially along the coasts of Sardinia.

choices.label: Not coastal-maritime
Thallus forming orbicular, usually confluent patches, often with a brighter yellow marginal zone. On shaded, steeply inclined, rain-protected surfaces
choices.name: Coppinsiella fiumana (Zahlbr.) I.V. Frolov
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, areolate, bright orange-yellow, lemon-yellow, ochre-yellow or orange, rarely white, often with a brighter yellow, 1-1.5 mm wide marginal zone, forming orbicular, (5-)13-18(-37) mm wide patches, several thalli often merging to cover larger areas, often rimmed by a thin white to light orange, fimbriate prothallus. Areoles angular or rounded, (0.1-)0.2-0.6(-1) mm in diam., flat to convex, often granular at thallus margin, the granules (0.04-)0.08–0.22(-0.35) mm wide; central areoles often forming (0.4-)0.8-1.8(-3) mm thick, raised tufts with a thicker medulla. Cortex conspicuous, even, often with gaps resulting from dead algal cells, (10-)20-26(-42) µm high, formed of 3-7 layers of thin-walled isodiametrical cells, usually with large, more or less isodiametrical crystals of calcium oxalates; epinecral layer yellow-brown, (3-)6-13(-30) µm thick; medulla usually conspicuous (10-)17-28(-38) µm thick, formed by a prosoplectenchymatous tissue of thin-walled hyphae, with minute crystals. Apothecia often abundant, zeorine, at first immersed, becoming adnate to sessile, (0.3-)0.5-0.7(-1.1) mm across, with a flat to convex, orange, epruinose disc, a yellow to orange, paler, raised thalline margin, and an orange proper margin forming a parathecial ring. Thalline exciple (14-)40-54(-120) µm wide, corticate, formed of isodiametrical to elongated thin-walled cells; proper exciple (16-)27-47(-75) µm wide, colourless within, formed by thin-walled, almost isodiametrical cells in the uppermost part, of palisade prosoplectenchyma with thin-walled cells in lower part; epithecium yellow-brown, covered in colourless granular crystals, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, (50-)76-96(-150) µm high, inspersed with oil droplets; paraphyses usually branched, containing oil droplets, (1.5-)2(-4.5) µm thick in lower part, the apical cells (3.5–)5.5–8(–10) µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid or rarely partly rhomboid, (7.5-)10-13.5(-16) x (2.5-)5-7(-10) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2.5-)4.5-6(-7.5) µm. Pycnidia common, mostly marginal, forming brighter yellow-orange spots. Conidia ellipsoid, straight or rarely slightly curved or tear shaped, rarely bacilliform, (2-)3-3.5(-5) x (1-)1.7-2.2(-3.0) µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: parietin (major), emodin, fallacinal, parietinic acid and teloschistin (minor or traces). Note: on steeply inclined, rather shaded, rain-protected surfaces of calcareous rocks. Described from Fiume (Croatia) and known from several sites in Central Europe; to be looked for in Italy.

choices.label: Thallus forming irregular patches, without a brighter yellow marginal zone. On sunny surfaces wetted by rain
Apothecia persistently immersed in the thallus. Thallus thin, smooth, continuous or faintly rimose
choices.name: Variospora dalmatica (A. Massal.) Cl. Roux
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, ochraceous yellow to ochraceous orange, epruinose, smooth and subcontinuous or sometimes finely cracked, usually well-delimited, forming up to 3 cm wide patches. Apothecia frequent, 0.3-0.8(-1) mm across, persistently immersed in the thallus, with an initially flat, then sometimes convex, orange to brownish orange disc and a usually slightly paler, smooth, persistent margin. Epithecium orange, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 50-80 μm high; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells swollen, up to 4-6 μm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid to broadly ellipsoid, 9-15 x 5-10 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-5 μm (1/4-1/2 of spore length). Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a poorly known calcicolous species described from Dalmatia. The epithet dalmatica seems to have priority within a difficult and still not fully understood complex of related species found on a wide variety of calcareous substrata in exposed, rather eutrophicated situations. The records reported from Italy refer to the species in a very broad sense; several of them could refer to other species, such as V. dolomiticola, V. epierodens, V. placidia, V. schaereri, V. velana.

choices.label: Apothecia finally projecting. Thallus areolate, the areoles separated by large cracks
choices.name: Variospora dolomiticola (Hue) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, of angular, 0.4-1.2 mm wide, orange to yellow-orange areoles separated by deep fissures, rarely subcontinuous and finely cracked, usually well-delimited, sometimes with a black hypothallus, forming up to 3 cm wide patches. Cortex 25-95 μm thick, paraplectenchymatous, with yellowish orange crystals at the surface; medulla paraplectenchymatous; algal layer discontinuous. Apothecia zeorine, frequent, usually angular by mutual compression, 0.2-0.8(-1) mm across, at first immersed in the areoles, then subsessile, with an initially flat, then sometimes convex, orange to brownish orange disc and a usually slightly paler, smooth, persistent margin. Thalline exciple well-developed, with many algae; proper exciple 85–100 μm wide, prosoplectenchymatous; epithecium orange, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 50-90(-100) μm high; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells swollen, up to 4-6 μm wide; hypothecium colourless, sometimes with oil droplets, prosoplectenchymatous. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid to broadly ellipsoid, 9-13 x 5-10 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-5 μm (1/4-1/2 of spore length). Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a still poorly understood species, often considered as a synonym of V. velana, growing on dolomite and schists in upland areas, with optimum above the montane belt.

choices.label: Apothecia scarlet red, immersed in the areoles. Thallus forming small patches, up to 2 cm in diam.
choices.name: Caloplaca rubelliana (Ach.) Lojka
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, areolate, well-delimited, pinkish grey to cinnamon-red, forming up to 2,5 cm wide patches, sometimes with a grey prothallus. Areoles flat, smooth, up to 1.5 mm wide, the peripheral ones usually larger than the central ones. Cortex paraplectenchymatous, 10-30 µm thick; medulla poorly developed, dense. Apothecia frequent, immersed in the areoles, 0.2-0.5 mm across, with a scarlet red, at first often concave, then flat, epruinose disc and a persistent, but thin and poorly evident margin. Exciple of elongate to oval cells, prosoplectenchymatous below the hypothecium; epithecium orange, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 55-75 µm high; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, 1-1.5(-2) µm thick at base, at the apical cells 3-4 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (7-)8-11 x 4-7 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-5 µm, c. 1/3 of spore length. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a warm-temperate to subtropical, widespread lichen found on steeply inclined surfaces of hard, basic siliceous rocks (especially basalt), often with species of Peltula. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str. and could belong to Brownliella Y. Kondr. (Arup in litt.).

choices.label: Apothecia orange to orange-brown, not immersed in the areoles. Thallus usually several cm in diam.
Apothecia orange-brown, with chlorinated anthraquinones (at least fleeting C+ purple in section). Thallus dirty yellow to dirty yellowish-orange
choices.name: Gyalolechia flavovirescens (Wulfen) Søchting, Frödén & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, almost continuous to rimose-areolate, up to 0.5 mm thick, well-delimited, sometimes with a black prothallus when young, pale dirty yellow to dirty yellowish orange, sometimes with a greenish tinge. Cortex cellular, 15-22(-30) µm thick; algal layer continuous; medulla white, paraplectenchymatous Apothecia zeorine, adnate, 0.4-1.3 mm across, with a dark orange to brownish red (paler in young apothecia), flat to convex, epruinose disc, a persistent to usually disappearing thalline margin concolorous with thallus and a proper margin which is usually slightly paler than disc. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, of radiating hyphae; epithecium golden yellow, granular, K+ purple-red, C- or C+ purple; hymenium colourless, 70-100(-120) µm high, not inspersed; paraphyses unbranched or sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells slightly swollen, up to 3.5 µm wide; hypothecium colourless, not inspersed with oil droplets, prosoplectenchymatous. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (10-)12-18(-20.5) x (5.5-)7-9(-12) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (3.5-)4-8(-10) µm (1/2-1/3 of spore length). Pycnidia totally immersed, the ostiolar region orange. Conidia bacilliform, 2.5–5 x 1–1.5 μm, Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia C+ purple (reaction often poorly evident). Chemistry: thallus with fragilin (major), emodin, parietin and other anthraquinones (minor); apothecia with predominant parietin and variable, usually low amounts of chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a mainly temperate species with optimum on weakly calcareous sandstone and calciferous schists, on boulders and walls, with optimum at relatively low elevations.

choices.label: Apothecia and thallus orange, without chlorinated anthraquinones (C- in section)
Species of dry-warm sites, with a subsquamulose thallus often developing on a black hypothallus
choices.name: Squamulea subsoluta (Nyl.) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose to subsquamulose, episubstratic, bright orange to brownish yellow, of small, flat, c. 0.5 mm wide, scattered to contiguous, subsquamulose areoles developing on a black hypothallus, the marginal ones often crenulate-lobulate. Cortex paraplectenchymatous, 15-30 µm thick, inspersed with crystals of anthraquinones; medulla thin, inconspicuous. Apothecia zeorine, adnate, 0.2-0.6 mm across, with an orange to red-orange, flat to convex disc and a smooth, paler, persistent proper margin. Proper exciple paraplectenchymatous, brownish orange in outer part, colourless within, the pigmented parts K+ purple-red; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red, C-; hymenium colourless, 60-80 µm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched in upper part, c. 1.5 μm thick at mid-level, the apical cells slightly swollen, 2-3(-5) μm wide; hypothecium colourless, the lower part paraplectenchymatous, with 3-5 μm wide cells. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, broadly ellipsoid, (9-)10-13(-15) x (4-)5-7(-8) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-5 μm (1/4-1/2 of spore length). Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin, fallacinal, emodin, and teloschistin. Note: a mild-temperate to subtropical, widespread lichen found on steeply inclined, sunny surfaces of basic siliceous rocks, often with Peltula euploca, but less bound to seepage tracks.

choices.label: Species restricted to coastal situations, with a crustose, often weakly lobulate thallus without a black hypothallus
Thallus areolate-bullate to minutely subsquamulose, the areoles coarsely granular, the granules (70-)120-240(-380) μm in diam.
choices.name: Flavoplaca communis (Vondrák, Ríha, Arup & Søchting) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, yellow to yellow-orange, areolate-bullate to minutely subsquamulose, but sometimes consisting of dispersed, coarse granules only, esorediate. Areoles dispersed or contiguous and then overgrowing each other, forming thick crusts in luxuriant populations, (90-)115-165(-450) μm thick, (0•3-)0.4-1.2(-2•8) mm wide, usually coarsely granular; the granules (70-)120-240(-380) μm in diam. Cortex present, (5-)10-24(-46) μm thick. Apothecia frequent, zeorine, yellow-orange, (0.2-)0.4-0.8(-1.3) mm across, with a slightly concave to flat disc and a rather thick, often crenulated, paler or concolour margin. Exciple (40-)65-135(-210) μm wide, composed by a prominent amphithecium and a parathecium filling c. 1/3-1/2 of the total width; epithecium orange, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, (50-)55-80(-100) μm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched, the apical cells to (3-)4-6(-7) μm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, , cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 1-septate, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (10-)11.5-14.5(-18) x (4-)5.5-7.5(-9) μm, the septum (3)4-6(-7) μm thick (c. 1/4 of spore length). Pycnidia yellow-orange. Conidia (2-)2.5-3(-3•5) x 1-1.5(-2) μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a maritime species of siliceous seashore cliffs, closely related to F. maritima. The sample from Tuscany was collected at Punta Ala near Follonica.

choices.label: Thallus different, not granulose
Thallus ochraceous yellow to pale orange, of convex, knobby areoles, the margins never lobulate (areoles becoming smaller towards the margin)
choices.name: Flavoplaca maritima (B. de Lesd.) Arup, Frödén & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, ochraceous yellow to pale orange, rimose-areolate, the areoles convex, uneven and knobby, forming orbicular to irregular, extensive patches delimited by an orange prothallus, the margins not lobulate (areoles becoming smaller towards the thallus margin). Cortex paraplectenchymatous, K+ purple-red. Apothecia zeorine, yellow-orange, often clustered, sessile when young but soon raised and constricted at base, 0.5- 0.8(-1) mm across, with a flat slightly convex, orange disc, a slightly raised, smooth, often paler proper margin and a sometimes finally excluded thalline margin. proper exciple of radiating, thick-walled, tightly packed hyphae; epithecium orange-brown, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless; paraphyses somewhat moniliform, simple to branched, 1-2(-3.5) μm thick at mid-level, the apical cells swollen; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 10-16 x 5-8 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3.5-5.5 µm (c. 1/3 of spore length). Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a maritime-coastal species, often confused with F. marina, growing both on siliceous and calcareous rocks, known from the Atlantic coasts and also reported from Corsica (Roux & Coll. 2025). To be looked for in Italy, especially along the coasts of Sardinia.

choices.label: Thallus deep orange to orange-red, of mostly flat, not knobby areoles, the margins more or less distinctly lobulate

Prothallus often present. Apothecia more intensely coloured than thallus. Apothecial disc often of a different colour than margin. Apex of paraphyses strongly enlarged, 4-5(-7) μm thick. Ascospores 10.5-15(-18.5) x (3.7-)4.5-7(-8) μm
choices.name: Flavoplaca marina (Wedd.) Arup, Frödén & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, orange to orange-red, very variable, continuous to rimose-areolate in central parts, forming orbicular to more rarely irregular, up to 3 cm wide patches, sometimes delimited by a paler prothallus, the margins often indistinctly lobulate, the lobules 0.1-0.3 mm wide. Areoles (0.1-)0.2-0.7(-0.9) mm wide, mostly flat to slighty convex, not knobby, the marginal ones often longer than wide. Cortex paraplectenchymatous, K+ purple-red. Apothecia zeorine, yellow-orange, often clustered, sessile when young but soon raised and strongly constricted at base, (0.2-)0.4-1.2(-1.7) mm across, with a concave to slightly convex, often uneven, orange disc, a slightly raised, smooth, often paler proper margin and a flexuose to crenulate, sometimes finally excluded thalline margin. Thalline exciple up to 150 μm wide; proper exciple (25-)50-100(-120) μm wide, of radiating, thick-walled, tightly packed hyphae; epithecium orange-brown, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, (60-)70-95 μm high; paraphyses somewhat moniliform, simple to branched, 1-2(-3.5) μm thick at mid-level, the apical cells 4-7 μm wide; hypothecium colourless, sometimes inspersed with oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (9-)10.5-15(-18.5) x (3.7-)4.5-7(-8) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (1.8-)2.5-5(-6.5) μm (c. 1/3 of spore length). Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a Mediterranean-Atlantic species in Europe, reported also from North America, growing on basic siliceous rocks, more rarely on calciferous substrata in the salt-spray belt. According to Vondrák (in litt.), however, F. marina could be absent from Italy: the lichen with F. marina-appearance from siliceous shores in Sardinia and Sicily is in fact a member of Haloplaca; pending the publication of the new data, I still maintain these records under F. marina. See also note on F. ora.

choices.label: Prothallus absent. Apothecia and thallus of the same intensity of orange. Apex of paraphyses weakly enlarged, 1-2(-2.5) μm thick. Ascospores (9-)10-12 x 4-6 μm
choices.name: Flavoplaca ora (Poelt & Nimis) Arup, Frödén & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, homogeneously bright orange, areolate in central parts, the areoles flat to slightly convex, not knowby, more or less distinctly lobulate in marginal parts, forming irregular rosettes which are often confluent and cover large areas, without a distinct prothallus. Apothecia numerous, sparse or more often clustered, rounded or irregular, 0.2-0.8 mm across, with a more or less flat, deep orange disc, and a thin, usually somehow paler orange margin. Epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless; paraphyses 1-1.5 µm thick at mid-level, the apical cells weakly enlarged, 1-2(-2.5) μm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (9-)10-12 x 4-6 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-5 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a Mediterranean lichen found on siliceous, more rarely calcareous rocks near the sea, often associated with specimens identified as F. marina (see note on that species), apparently without transitional specimens.

choices.label: Lichenicolous on cyanolichens (usually Spilonema)
choices.name: Pachypeltis castellana (Räsänen) Søchting, Frödén & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, brownish orange, usually associated with cyanobacterial lichens, consisting of dispersed to crowded, flat to convex,sometimes weakly lobulate dull, epruinose, up to 1 mm wide areoles, without a distinct prothallus. Thallus paraplectenchymatous throughout; medulla I+ blue at least in basal parts. Apothecia zeorine, yellow-orange, dispersed or grouped, round, 0.3-1(-3) mm across, at first adnate then sessile and constricted at base, with a flat to slightly convex disc, a paler, thick, waxy, shining thalline margin, and often a thin, reddish orange parathecial ring; the apothecial margin is sometimes partly blue-grey to greenish due to the presence of the Cinereorufa-green pigment, which reacts K-, N+ purple. Thalline exciple corticate, c. 20 μm thick; proper exciple laterally expanded; epithecium brownish yellow, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 65-70 µm high; paraphyses free, slender, sometimes submoniliform in upper part, the apical cells 4-5 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, narrowly clavate, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (9-)10-13(-15) x (3.5-)5-7(-8) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) rather short, 2-3.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997); apothecia and parts of thallus sometimes with the Cinereorufa-green pigment. Note: on steep rock faces of mineral-rich schists with variable contents of calcium, often growing on cyanobacterial lichens (Spilonema); widespread in the Holarctic region, with scattered records from the Alps, outside the Italian territory: to be looked for in the Italian Alps.

choices.label: Not on cyanolichens
On epilithic lichens
On endolithic lichens
On maritime Hydropunctaria species
choices.name: Flavoplaca microthallina (Wedd.) Arup, Frödén & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose-microsquamulose, episubstratic, lemon-yellow to yellow-orange, consisting of scattered to imbricate, 0.3-0.5(-2) mm wide, rounded, flat to convex, sometimes isidia-like areoles/squamules, forming up to 2-3 cm wide patches. Cortex paraplectenchymatous with thin-walled cells. Apothecia zeorine, yellow-orange, sessile and constricted at base, 0.4-1.2(-1.6) mm across, with a flat to convex disc, a paler, minutely crenulate proper margin, and a conspicuous, mostly uneven to crenulate thalline margin. Thalline exciple 25-125(-175) μm wide; proper exciple (25-)40-60(-75) μm wide, of radiating, thick-walled, tightly packed hyphae; epithecium yellow-orange, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 75-90(-100) μm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched, somewhat moniliform in upper part, 1-2 μm thick at mid-level, the apical cells 3-6(-7) μm wide; hypothecium colourless, 30-80 μm high, rarely inspersed with oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (10-)12-15(-17) x (4-)6-8 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-6 µm (c. 1/4 of spore length). Pycnidia immersed, orange. Conidia narrowly ellipsoid, 2.5-3.2 x 1-1.2 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a mainly Atlantic species in Europe, also known from North America, confined to the salt-spray belt, in the mesic supralittoral zone where it often grows on Hydropunctaria-species; in Italy it is known from a single station in northwestern Sardinia (Punta Falcone).

choices.label: Not on Hydropunctaria
Ascospores markedly thickened at apex. On Kuettlingeria cretensis in the Mediterranean belt
choices.name: Caloplaca adelphoparasitica Nimis & Poelt
choices.description: Thallus crustose, areolate, parasitic on the grey thalli of Kuettlingeria cretensis, consisting of roundish, up to 5 mm wide islands, which often merge into larger patches, attacking the areoles of the host one after the other. Areoles thin, irregularly angular, pale pinkish-orange, flat, mostly up to 0.5 mm in diam. Cortex paraplectenchymatous; medulla loose, poorly developed. Apothecia mostly biatorine, but often sitting on a thick algal layer, some algae penetrating in the weakly differentiated exciple, usually sparse, immersed to sessile, mostly solitary in the areoles, 0.2-0.4 mm across, with a flat to slightly convex, pale reddish-orange disc, and an initially thick, then thinner and finally excluded margin of the same colour as the disc. Proper exciple thin, unclearly radiate-paraplectenchymatous, more or less swollen, the hyphae with rounded to elongated, 3-7 µm thick cell lumina; epithecium brownish, with a finely granulose epipsamma, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, c. 80 µm high; paraphyses robust, strongly coherent, 1.5-2 µm thick, often apically branched and progressively thicker upwards; hypothecium colourless. Asci (6-)8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid, the apical wall thicker than the lateral one, and therefore lumina somehow heart-shaped, 10.5-12 x 6.5-8 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2-4 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a well-distinguished calcicolous species growing on Kuettlingeria cretensis, also known from Turkey, to be sought for throughout the Mediterranean, in coastal situations, wherever the host is found, but certainly not common. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: Ascospores not markedly thickened at apex. On other hosts
Thallus with a well developed medulla reacting I+ blue. On aspicilioid lichens in the alpine belt
Thallus with a poorly developed medulla reacting I-. Most frequent on crustose lichens below the alpine belt
Thallus and apothecia orange- to ochraceous-yellow
choices.name: Pachypeltis insularis (Poelt) Vondrák & I.V.Frolov
choices.description: Thallus orange- to ochraceous yellow, of 0.2-0.6 mm wide, subsquamulose areoles, or reduced to small granules-areoles around the apothecia, forming 2-4 mm wide spots on the thalli of Aspicilia species. Upper cortex weakly paraplectenchymatous; medulla white, loosely paraplectenchymatous, I+ blue (reaction best visible at the base of old apothecia). Apothecia zeorine, usually in small groups and deformed by mutual compression, (0.2-)0.4-0.6(-0.8) mm across, with an orange-brown, flat to slightly convex, rough disc, and a thick, paler, smooth proper margin; a reduced thalline margin is sometimes visible in young apothecia. Epithecium brownish orange, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 80-90 μm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched, the apical cells up to 5 μm wide; hypothecium colourless, of strongly conglutinated hyphae, I+ blue in lowermost part. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid to ellipsoid, (9-)10-13(-15) x 6-8(-9) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (1.5-)2-4 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: on calcareous schists, parasitic on Aspicilia candida and A. polychroma; known from South Tyrol, but probably more widespread in the Alps.

choices.label: Thallus and apothecia scarlet red
choices.name: Caloplaca anchon-phoeniceon Poelt & Clauzade
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, parasitic on aspicilioid lichens, deep orange-red to scarlet red, somehow glossy, consisting of up to 0.6 mm wide, dispersed, convex areoles, sometimes reduced to a collar surrounding the apothecia. Cortex c. 15 µm thick, poorly delimited, paraplectenchymatous; medulla well-developed, I+ blue. Apothecia zeorine, scattered to crowded, round to angular, sessile and slightly constricted at base, 0.5-0.9 mm across, with a deep red-orange to carmine red, flat to slightly convex disc (slightly darker than the thallus) and an initially thick and prominent, usually smooth proper margin concolorous with thallus. Thalline exciple with algae almost to the edge; proper exciple slightly fan-shaped at the periphery; epithecium brownish red, with a coarse epipsamma reacting K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 50-70 µm high; paraphyses sparingly branched, c. 1 µm thick at base, the apical cells only slightly thickened, up to 1.5 µm wide; hypothecium colourless, inspersed with oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (11-)13-15 x (5-)6-8 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (3-)4-5.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with unidentified anthraquinones Note: a species with minute thalli and one to several sessile apothecia, both bright red; parasitic on silicicolous Aspicilia-species at high elevations; widespread in the Alps, but rare. Never reported from Italy but known from neighbouring countries; to be looked for in the Alps. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: On calcicolous epilithic lichens
On silicicolous epilithic lichens
Thallus often slightly lobulate at margins, forming well-delimited, to 1 cm wide, round but often confluent patches on the thalli of different crustose lichens, but usually not on Pyrenodesmia
choices.name: Athallia inconnexa (Nyl.) S.Y. Kondr. & Lőkös
choices.description: Thallus crustose, yellow to (more rarely) orange yellow, starting the life-cycle on different calcicolous lichens, from granulose to irregularly areolate, often slightly lobulate at margins, forming well-delimited, to 1 cm wide, round to very irregular, often coalescing patches. Cortex paraplectenchymatous, orange brown in outer part, colourless in inner part, the pigmented parts K+ red, of thin-walled cells; medulla poorly developed, I-. Apothecia frequent, zeorine, immersed when young but soon sessile, 0.3-0.7(-1) mm across, with a flat to slightly convex, yellow to yellow-orange disc and a somewhat paler, persistent margin. Epithecium orange, with orange-brown crystals soluble in K, 10-15 μm high, K+ purple-red, C-; hymenium colourless, 60-85 μm high; paraphyses mostly unbranched, c. 1.5-2.5 μm thick at mid-level, the apical cells up to 7 μm wide. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 10-13(-14) x 6-8 μm, the septum 3-5(-8) μm (1/3-1/2 of spore length). Photobiont: chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a mild-temperate species found on the top of isolated calcareous boulders and rock outcrops, on calcareous rocks wetted by rain in sunny situations, especially common on Acarospora cervina and Circinaria calcarea. The species, as currently understood, probably belongs to Athallia, but the poorly developed type material probably belongs in Variospora (Vondrák & al. 2016), so that the nomenclature of this lichen is likely to change in the near future. The relationships with A. necator still remain to be clarified.

choices.label: Thallus not lobulate, distinctly areolate to granulose, starting the life-cycle on species of Pyrenodesmia
Thallus granular to granular-verrucose, starting the life-cycle on Pyrenodesmia variabilis
choices.name: Variospora velana (A. Massal.) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, starting the life-cycle on the thalli of Pyrenodesmia variabilis, granular to granular-areolate, ochraceous yellow to brownish orange, epruinose, often developed only around the apothecia. Apothecia frequent, zeorine, crowded, 0.5-1.2(-2) mm across, not immersed in the thallus, with an orange disc and a usually paler, persistent margin. Epithecium orange, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, swollen at apex; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid to broadly ellipsoid, 9-15 x 5-10 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-6 μm (1/4-1/2 of spore length). Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a member of the a difficult and still poorly known group of closely related species, starting the life-cycle on the thalli of Pyrenodesmia variabilis (Roiux & Coll. 2025), apparently with a wide altitudinal range. Older records are untrustworthy and may be hidden under those of V. dalmatica.

choices.label: Thallus finely areolate, starting the life-cycle on Pyrenodesmia chalybea
choices.name: Variospora placidia (A. Massal.) Cl. Roux
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, starting the life-cycle on the thalli of Pyrenodesmia chalybaea, finely rimose-areolate, ochraceous yellow to brownish orange, epruinose, rather thick, the areoles angular, smooth, flat. Apothecia frequent, zeorine, 0.5-2 mm across, not immersed in the thallus, with an orange disc and a usually paler, persistent margin. Epithecium orange, granular K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, swollen at apex; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid to broadly ellipsoid, (9-)10-13 x (5-)7-10 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (3-)4-6.5 μm (1/4-1/2 of spore length). Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a member of a poorly understood group, described from the surroundings of Verona and probably much more widespread. According to Roux & Coll. (2025) it starts the life-cycle on the thalli of Pyrenodesmia chalybaea and is quite common in southern France.

choices.label: On silicicolous species of Candelariella
choices.name: Athallia vitellinaria (Szatala) ined.
choices.description: Thallus not evident or crustose, orange, very much reduced and visible only around the apothecia, developing on silicicolous species of Candelariella, especially C. vitellina. Medulla I-. Apothecia zeorine, usually numerous and clustered, round to angular by mutual compression, (0.3-)0.5-1(1.5) mm across, with a flat to slightly convex, orange disc, a thin, slightly paler, only initially raised, finally sometimes excluded margin and sometimes a poorly developed thalline margin visible only on the underside of young apothecia.
