choices.description: Thallus crustose, usually episubstratic but sometimes poorly evident, yellow to yellow-orange, areolate or of scattered granules, usually developed only near the apothecia, Cortex thin, indistinct, with yellowish orange crystals; algal layer continuous, Apothecia zeorine, frequent, sessile, (0.4-)0.5-0.7(-1) mm across, often crowded, with an orange to brown-orange disc, a slightly paler orange proper margin and sometimes a poorly developed, warted thalline margin which tends to disappear in older apothecia. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, orange-brown in outer part, colourless within, (50-)80-100 μm thick, the pigmented part K+ purple-red; epithecium with numerous yellow-brown crystals, K+ purple-red, C-; hymenium colourless, 85–100(–120) μm high; paraphyses simple to sparingly branched and moniliform in upper part, the apical up to 4-6 μm wide; hypothecium colourless, sometimes with a few oil droplets, prosoplectenchymatous. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, narrowly ellipsoid, (13-)15-20(-22) x (4.5-)6-9(-10) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 1-3 μm (<1/8 of spore length). Photobiont: chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and apothecia K+ purple-red, C-, KC-, P-. Chemistry: thallus and apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a mild-temperate to subtropical species, often found on calcareous walls, perhaps parasitic of Verrucaria nigrescens when young, very much misunderstood in the past (see note on X. lactea). Recently, this taxon has been considered to be complex and to contain at least four lineages (Vondrák & al. 2011). Very similar is Caloplaca bisagnonis B. de Lesd., described from Liguria, which, according to Roux & Coll. (2025), differs in the smaller spores measuring 11-15(-17) x 4-7.5 μm, and the longer septum (2-4 μm). Several records from siliceous rocks, such as those of Nimis & Tretiach (1999) from Abruzzo and Basilicata, refer to X. diffusa.

choices.label: Apothecia ochraceous yellow. Thallus well-developed, whitish grey, areolate or rimose-areolate
choices.name: Caloplaca spotornonis B. de Lesd.
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, whitish grey, rimose-areolate or areolate, rarely thin and poorly evident. Apothecia irregularly rounded, 0.3-0.7(-1.5) mm across, with an ochraceous yellow to pale yellowish red, flat to convex disc, and a paler, ochraceous yellow, persistent proper margin; a thalline margin is sometimes visible at the base of young apothecia. Epithecium yellowish brown, c. 20 µm high, inspersed with granules, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 55-60 µm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells swollen; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, 12-20 x 5-7 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2-3 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red. Chemistry: thallus probably without lichen substances; apothecia with an unknown set of anthraquinones. Note: on horizontal to subvertical surfaces of non-calciferous schists in sunny situations. This species was synonymised by Nimis & Martellos (2008) with Rufoplaca arenaria, but according to Roux & coll. (2014) it clearly differs in the well-developed thallus, the ochraceous yellow apothecia and the somewhat longer spores. It is hitherto known only from Liguria and Southern France, and it probably belongs to Rufoplaca.

choices.label: Apothecia bright orange to orange red (sometimes blackening when old). Thallus inapparent or well-developed
Lichenicolous on Miriquidica nigroleprosa
choices.name: Caloplaca magni-filii Poelt
choices.description: Thallus crustose, poorly evident, completely immersed in the thalli of Miriquidica nigroleprosa. Apothecia zeorine, sparse, 0.2-0.5 mm across, with a rust-red to orange-red, flat to convex, rough disc, and a slightly raised, sometimes greyish-orange, finally often excluded proper margin. Proper exciple relatively thick, with algae in lower part, I+ distinctly blue; epithecium brownish orange, K+ red, C+ purple (section!); hymenium colourless, 50-70 µm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched, the apical cells only slightly swollen; hypothecium colourless. Asci (6-)8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid, 10-12 x 5-6 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2.5-4 µm thick, or subglobose, c. 10 µm wide, the equatorial thickening 2.5-3.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple (the last reaction best observed in thick sections under the microscope). Chemistry: apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: exclusively parasite on thalli of the silicicolous Miriquidica nigroleprosa, usually from the high montane to the lower alpine belt; widespread in the European parts of the Holarctic, including the Alps, but rare; not reported from Italy, to be looked for in the Alps. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: Not lichenicolous, or on other lichens
Apothecial disc dark reddish brown tending to turn dark red to black with age, contrasting with the paler margin
Apothecial disc not turning dark with age
Apothecia with a thalline margin when young. Ascospores 10-13 x 4-5(-6) μm
choices.name: Rufoplaca scotoplaca (Nyl.) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, thin, continuous to rimose-areolate, ash-grey to dark grey-brown, often delimited by a dark prothallus, the areoles 0.2-0.4 mm wide, 0.1-0.2 mm thick, irregular, flat to uneven, separated by very thin, often indistinct cracks. Apothecia appressed to sessile, circular to angular by mutual compression, 0.2-0.4(-0.5) mm across, with a flat to slightly convex, bright to dark rust-red, finally rarely blackening disc, a thin, mostly persistent, at first paler, then concolorous (or blackened), rarely excluded proper margin, and a grey thalline margin which is evident at least in young apothecia. Proper exciple brownish yellow in outer part, colourless within; epithecium brownish yellow, inspersed with orange-yellow crystals of anthraquinones reacting K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless or yellowish in upper part, 60-70 μm high, amyloid; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched in upper part, c. 1.7 μm thick at base, the apical cells swollen, 4-5 μm wide; hypothecium 20-50 μm high, colourless to greyish, I+ dark blue. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, narrowly ellipsoid, 10-13 x (3-)4-6(-8) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2-)3-4(-5) μm, 1/4-1/3 of spore length. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ weakly violet in section, C- or C+ violet (reaction visible only in sections) KC-, P-; disc of apothecia K+ purple-red, C-. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; disc of apothecia with non-chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: at least in Southern Europe this lichen of basic, hard siliceous rocks has been much misunderstood; several earlier Italian records, especially those from outside the Alps, need confirmation, as well as those from Sardinia (see Nimis & Poelt 1987: 74).

choices.label: Apothecia without a thalline margin. Ascospores 12-20 x 5-8 µm
choices.name: Caloplaca ligustica B. de Lesd.
choices.description: Thallus crustose, thinly episubstratic, pale grey, continuous to rimose. Apothecia biatorine, 0.3-1.5 mm across, usually crowded and sometimes deformed by mutual compression, with a flat to convex, dark reddish brown disc tending to turn dark red to black in older apothecia, the disc contrasting with the margin, which remains dark orange-red. Epithecium brownish orange, K+ purple-red; hymenium and hypothecium pale reddish; paraphyses branched in upper part, the apical cells 3-4 µm wide. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, narrowly ellipsoid, (12-)14-20 x 5-8 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 1.5-2.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecial disc K+ purple-red. Chemistry: apothecia with chemosyndrome C2 of Søchting (1997): absence of parietin and fragilin and traces of citreorosein and emodinal. Note: on schists in open habitats, on dry surfaces with a short water flow after rain; poorly understood, but probably a good species, known from Italy, France, and the Iberian Peninsula. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.: the type specimen (PRA-V 03097; syntype?) was morphologically appraised and belongs to Rufoplaca (Vondrák in litt.).

choices.label: Proper exciple of apothecia with a dark rim (visible at least in section)
Proper exciple without a dark rim (a critical group which needs further study)

Thallus poorly developed, forming paler patches on the thalli or other lichens, or inapparent, without the Sedifolia-grey pigment. Apothecia 0.3-0.8(-1) mm across, sessile C+ purple, with chlorinated anthraquinones
choices.name: Erichansenia epithallina (Lynge) S. Y. Kondr., Kärnefelt & A. Thell
choices.description: Thallus crustose, endosubstratic, forming paler patches on the thallus of the host lichens, or inapparent. Apothecia zeorine, 0.3-0.8(-1) mm across, often clustered in small groups, sessile, slightly to strongly constricted at base, with a flat to convex, dark orange to rusty red, finely granulose disc and a persistent to excluded, smooth to rough, often darkened margin. Proper exciple 20-120 μm wide, with many algal cells, the outer part corticate, almost black in mature apothecia, the inner part prosoplectenchymatous, hyaline, not amyloid; epithecium yellowish orange to ferruginous red, K+ purple-red, C+ purple in section; hymenium colourless, 50-60 μm high, not amyloid; paraphyses branched in upper part, the apical cells swollen, 3-4 μm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci (6-)8-spored, clavate, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid, (9-)11-13(-14) x 5.5-8 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2-4 μm (c. 1/2-1/3 of spore length). Thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple. Chemistry: apothecia with chlorinated and unchlorinated anthraquinones: 7-Cl-emodin (major), parietin (subdominant), emodin (minor), 7-Cl-emodinal (minor), 2 unknown compounds (minor). Note: a rather continental species found on sunny surfaces of siliceous rocks, e.g. on isolated boulders in grasslands, restricted to dry-continental Alpine valleys in Italy.

choices.label: Thallus well-developed, pale to dark grey, starting the life-cycle on Rinodina oxydata, later autonomous, with the Sedifolia-grey pigment. Apothecia 0.1-0.3 mm across, immersed to adnate, C-, with unchlorinated anthraquinones
choices.name: Rufoplaca griseomarginata Vondrák & S. Svoboda
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, rimose-areolate, up to 100 μm thick, pale to dark grey, initially lichenicolous on Rinodina oxydata, later forming independent, up to 1 cm wide patches. Apothecia 0.1-0.3 mm across, usually immersed in the thallus or adnate, finally sometimes slightly raised above the thallus surface, with an orange disc, the proper exciple orange and K+ purple-red in the part adjacent to disc, but grey and K+ violet (Sedifolia-grey pigment) in outer part; thalline exciple present but thin or indistinct. Epithecium orange, K+ purple-red; hymenium and hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 11-14 x 4.5-6.5 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) short, 2.5-3 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ faintly violet, C-, KC-, P-; apothecial disc K+ purple-red. Chemistry: thallus and proper exciple with the Sedifolia grey pigment; epithecium with parietin and 2 unidentified non-chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a recently-described species of base-rich siliceous outcrops and stones in rather humid but sunny situations at low elevations, which starts the life-cycle on Rinodina oxydata, later becoming autonomous. It is hitherto known from the Czech Republic, Greece, Turkey and Iran (Vondrák & al. 2022). To be looked for in Italy.

choices.label: Apothecia orange
Apothecia orange-red, rust-red, or dark reddish brown
Apothecia without a macroscopically evident thalline margin. Thallus rimose-areolate, pale to dark grey, not verruculose
choices.name: Rufoplaca subpallida (H. Magn.) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, rather thin to rather thick but usually not verruculose, rimose-areolate, pale to dark grey, forming irregular patches, sometimes delimited by a thin, black prothallus. Cortex inconspicuous, paraplectenchymatous, the upper part K+ and N+ very weakly violet. Apothecia zeorine, usually crowded, at first partially immersed, then broadly sessile, round to angular by mutual compression, (0.1-)0.4-0.7(-1.2) mm across, with an initially concave, then flat, dark orange disc and a persistent, smooth, raised, slightly paler proper margin; thalline margin usually not evident macroscopically, rarely present at the base of apothecia. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, with anthraquinone crystals; epithecium inspersed with orange-yellow crystals of anthraquinones reacting K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 75-85(-110) μm high; paraphyses simple to sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells up to 5 μm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, narrowly ellipsoid, (10-)12-19(-20) x 4-6(-7) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2.5-)3-4 μm. Pycnidia black in upper part. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ weakly violet in section, C- or C+ violet, KC-, P-; disc of apothecia K+ purple-red, C-. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; disc of apothecia with unchlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a cool-temperate to arctic-alpine lichen found on mineral-rich siliceous rocks, sometimes parasitic on other lichens (Aspicilia, Rhizocarpon, brown Xanthoparmelia-species); many Mediterranean records (e.g. from the Iberian Peninsula) are probably wrong. The species has been often considered as a synonym of “Caloplaca” oxfordensis J. Hedrick, a taxon described from North America, but molecular data indicate that the two species are different (Arup & al. 2013).

choices.label: Thallus with a macroscopically evident thalline margin. Thallus thick, dark grey to blackish grey, often verruculose
choices.name: Rufoplaca tristiuscula (H. Magn.) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, rather thick, dark grey to blackish grey, rimose-areolate and often verruculose, forming large patches. Cortex paraplectenchymatous; medulla poorly evident. Apothecia zeorine, sessile, round to angular by mutual compression, 0.5-1.2 mm across, with an initially concave, then flat, orange to dark orange disc, a persistent, smooth, thin, distinctly paler proper margin and a dark grey, usually well-evident, only finally sometimes excluded thalline margin. Thalline exciple with abundant algae; proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, with anthraquinone crystals; epithecium inspersed with orange-yellow crystals of anthraquinones reacting K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless; paraphyses simple to sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells up to 5 μm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, narrowly ellipsoid, 10-16 x 4.5-7 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2.5-4 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ weakly violet in section, C- or C+ violet, KC-, P-; disc of apothecia K+ purple-red. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; disc of apothecia with unchlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a poorly known species described from Sweden, growing on base-rich siliceous rocks in subalpine-alpine areas, also reported from the Austrian Alps; the Italian sample, identified by J. Poelt, was collected by Buschardt in Val Venosta at c. 500 m.

choices.label: Apothecial disc dark reddish brown tending to turn dark red to black with age. Ascospore septum (2-)3-4(-5) μm, 1/4-1/3 of spore length
choices.name: Rufoplaca scotoplaca (Nyl.) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, thin, continuous to rimose-areolate, ash-grey to dark grey-brown, often delimited by a dark prothallus, the areoles 0.2-0.4 mm wide, 0.1-0.2 mm thick, irregular, flat to uneven, separated by very thin, often indistinct cracks. Apothecia appressed to sessile, circular to angular by mutual compression, 0.2-0.4(-0.5) mm across, with a flat to slightly convex, bright to dark rust-red, finally rarely blackening disc, a thin, mostly persistent, at first paler, then concolorous (or blackened), rarely excluded proper margin, and a grey thalline margin which is evident at least in young apothecia. Proper exciple brownish yellow in outer part, colourless within; epithecium brownish yellow, inspersed with orange-yellow crystals of anthraquinones reacting K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless or yellowish in upper part, 60-70 μm high, amyloid; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched in upper part, c. 1.7 μm thick at base, the apical cells swollen, 4-5 μm wide; hypothecium 20-50 μm high, colourless to greyish, I+ dark blue. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, narrowly ellipsoid, 10-13 x (3-)4-6(-8) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2-)3-4(-5) μm, 1/4-1/3 of spore length. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ weakly violet in section, C- or C+ violet (reaction visible only in sections) KC-, P-; disc of apothecia K+ purple-red, C-. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; disc of apothecia with non-chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: at least in Southern Europe this lichen of basic, hard siliceous rocks has been much misunderstood; several earlier Italian records, especially those from outside the Alps, need confirmation, as well as those from Sardinia (see Nimis & Poelt 1987: 74).

choices.label: Apothecial disc not turning dark with age. Ascospore septum 1-3(-3.5) μm , max 1/5 of spore length
Apothecia bright rust-red, with a rather thick, orange to red margin. Ascospores 10-18 x 4-6(-8) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (1.5-)2-3.5 μm
choices.name: Rufoplaca arenaria (Pers.) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, indistinct or very thin, pale grey to grey-brown, often developing on other crustose lichens. Cortex with the Sedifolia-grey pigment (K+ faintly violet in sections); medulla poorly evident. Apothecia common, (0.3-)0.5-1(-1.5) mm across, with a bright rust-red, flat to finally slightly convex disc becoming darker and brownish orange with age and a slightly paler, raised proper margin. Epithecium brownish orange, granular, K+ purple-red; hymenium and hypothecium colourless; paraphyses gradually broadening to 3-4 μm at apex. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, narrowly ellipsoid, 10-18 x 4-6(-8) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (1.5-)2-3.5 μm, c. 1/5 of spore length. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P- (but section of cortex, when present, K+ faintly violet, N+ red); apothecial disc and proper margin K+ purple-red, C-. Chemistry: cortex with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; epithecium and proper margin of apothecia with unchlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a holarctic lichen found on calciferous siliceous rocks, including walls, often overgrowing other crustose lichens; on the whole, a heterogeneous taxon in need of revision.

choices.label: Apothecia orange-red, with a thin margin concolorous with disc or paler. Ascospores 9-14 x 3-4 μm the equatorial thickening 1-2 μm
choices.name: Rufoplaca rubroaurantiaca (B. de Lesd.) Cl. Roux
choices.description: Thallus crustose, thinly episubstratic, whitish grey, often poorly visible. Apothecia cryptolecanorine to zeorine, sessile, irregularly rounded, 0.2-0.7 mm across, with an orange-red, flat to slightly convex disc, a concolorous or paler, raised proper margin, and a thalline margin which is usually developed only at the base of the apothecium and is soon excluded. Epithecium yellowish brown, inspersed with granules, 10-15 µm thick, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless 55-85 µm high, sometimes inspersed with a few oil droplets, I+ blue; paraphyses mostly simple; hypothecium colourless, 25-50 µm high, sometimes inspersed with a few oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, narrowly ellipsoid, 9-14 x 3-4(-6) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) short, 1-2 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red. Chemistry: thallus probably without lichen substances or with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; apothecia with an unknown set of non-chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a poorly known silicicolous species, a member of the difficult Rufoplaca arenaria-group characterised by the smaller spores with a thinner septum, known only from Italy, Switzerland and the French Alps (Dauphinè). The record from Valle d'Aosta (see Nimis 1993: 182) requires confirmation.

choices.label: Thallus chalky white, thick, areolate, with dark rust-red apothecia, growing on calcareous rocks
choices.name: Kuettlingeria erythrocarpa (Pers.) I.V. Frolov, Vondrák & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, chalky white, up to 0.7 mm thick, of flattened, angular areoles, the marginal ones sometimes elongate, giving the thallus a subplacodioid appearance, forming well-delimited, orbicular up to c. 5 cm wide patches, sometimes surrounded by a thin, dark prothallus. Cortex up to 60 μm thick, with abundant small crystals; medulla white. Apothecia frequent, lecanorine/zeorine, developing in the centre of areoles and in the central part of thallus, 0.4-1.5(-2) mm across, immersed to subsessile, with a flat, dark red to rust-red disc, a rust-red to orange (paler than disc) proper margin, and a finally often excluded, white thalline margin of variable thickness. Proper exciple orange in outer part, colourless within, the pigmented parts K+ purple-red, C+ purple; epithecium orange, K+ purple-red, C+ purple; hymenium colourless, 65-100 μm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched in upper part, not distinctly capitate; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 12-16(-18) x 6-9(-10) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (3-)5-8 μm, up to 1/4 of spore length. Pycnidia common, immersed, appearing as dark dots. Conidia narrowly ellipsoid to bacilliform. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple (both disc and proper margin). Chemistry: thallus without lichen substances or with low amounts of the Sedifolia-grey pigment; apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones in both margin and disc: 7-chloroemodin (major), fragilin and emodin (minor), sometimes traces of parietin. Note: a mainly Mediterranean species also occurring in warm habitats of the submediterranean belt found on limestone, dolomite, calciferous sandstone, much more rarely mortar and brick, on horizontal to weakly inclined faces wetted by rain, with optimum in natural habitats at low elevations.

choices.label: Lichens with a different combination of characters
Apothecia with a persistent thalline margin, concolorous with thallus (brown or grey)
Apothecia without thalline margin, or thalline margin much darker than thallus
Lichenicolous on Candelariella vitellina
choices.name: Pisutiella grimmiae (Nyl.) S. Y. Kondr., L. Lőkös & E. Farkas
choices.description: Thallus mostly immersed in that of the host, rarely visible externally as small, brown granules, otherwise reduced to the margin of apothecia. Apothecia lecanorine, (0.3-)0.5-0.8(-1.3) mm across, at first immersed, then subsessile, with a flat to convex, cinnamom-red to brown-red disc and a thick, dark grey-brown, finally sometimes almost excluded thalline margin. Thalline excipe corticate, of thick-walled hyphae; proper exciple paraplectenchymatous laterally, prosoplectenchymatous below the hypothecium; epithecium orange-brown, granular, K+ purple; hymenium colourless, 70-85 µm high, amyloid; paraphyses often sparingly branched in upper part, c. 1.5 μm wide at mid-level, the apical cells swollen, up to 5(-7) μm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid to broadly ellipsoid, (9-)10-14 x 5-7 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2.5-)3-4 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecial disc K+ purple. Chemistry: thallus without lichen substances; unidentified anthraquinones in the epithecium. Note: a holarctic, temperate to boreal-montane lichen, whose ecology and distribution are narrower than those of its host. It occurs throughout the country, exceptionally also in the Mediterranean belt, sometimes on walls, but, contrary to the host, is absent from heavily disturbed habitats.

choices.label: Not on Candelariella vitellina
Thallus very thick, subsquamulose to verrucose-areolate
Thallus thin, areolate
Proper margin of apothecia thin and poorly visible, not forming a ring around the thalline margin
choices.name: Caloplaca thracopontica Vondrák & Šoun
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, grey to dark grey, usually covered in 0.1-0.4 mm wide pustules or lobules, often forming large patches, delimited by a lead-grey prothallus. Cortex conspicuous, grey in upper part and colourless in lower part, paraplectenchymatous, usually with a thick epinecral layer. Apothecia lecanorine, (0.3-)0.7-1(-1.5) mm across, with an orange to dark red, flat disc, and a raised, grey thalline margin. Proper exciple very thin, prosoplectenchymatous; epithecium orange, inspersed with granules of anthraquinones, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 60-110 µm high: paraphyses branched and anastomosing in upper part, 1.5-2.5 µm thick at mid-level, the apical cells to 5(-6.5) µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid to rarely narrowly ellipsoid, (10-)11-14(-15.5) x (3-)5-7(-10) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2.5-)5-7 µm, 1/3-1/2 of spore length. Pycnidia dark. Conidia bacilliform, 2.5-5.5 x 1-1.5 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and thalline margin of apothecia K+ faintly violet, C-, KC-, P- (reaction best visible on a thick section under the microscope); apothecial disc K+ purple-red. C-. Chemistry: thallus and thalline margin of apothecia with the Sedifolia-grey pigment: apothecial disc with parietin (major), plus low concentrations of teloschistin, fallacinal, parietinic acid and emodin. Note: on base-rich siliceous rocks, especially on basalt, not uncommon at least in parts of Tyrrhenian Italy. A lichen like this, belonging to the difficult C. cerina-complex, was often called Caloplaca chlorina by South European authors. The application of the epithet chlorina was very controversial until Wetmore (1996) solved the problem by examining the type material. Non-isidiate, fruiting specimens from Central and Southern Italy collected at low elevations on basic siliceous rocks, were provisionally called Caloplaca cerinoides (Anzi) Jatta by Nimis (1993: 159), but according to Vondrák (in litt.), who examined material of this species collected by Anzi, this is a probable synonym of C. atroflava. The specimens in TSB agree quite well with C. thracopontica, described from the Black Sea Region.

choices.label: Proper margin of apothecia well-developed, forming a dark or orange parathecial ring
Apothecia with a blackish proper exciple reacting K+ violet in section (with Sedifolia-grey pigment)
choices.name: Caloplaca conglomerata (Bagl.) Jatta
choices.description: Thallus squamulose to areolate-verrucose, grey, lead-grey to almost black in sun-forms, olive-grey when wet, the areoles/squamules crowded, often imbricate, 0.3-1 mm wide, smooth. Cortex paraplectenchymatous, K+ faintly violet; medulla white, without granules. Apothecia zeorine/lecanorine, adnate, 0.5-1.5 mm across, with a yellow-orange to dark orange, flat to convex, epruinose disc, a brown to black (devoid of anthraquinones) proper margin forming an excipular ring between disc and thalline margin, and a usually persistent, slightly raised, often lobulate-crenulate thalline margin. Proper exciple of elongate to oval cells, K+ violet; epithecium orange, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 55-75 µm high; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells slightly swollen, 2-3 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 9-16 x 4-8 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2.5-)3-4(-5.5) µm (c. 1/3 of spore length). Pycnidia black, totally immersed. Conidia 4-6 x c. 1 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ faintly violet in section, C- or C+ violet, KC-, P-; disc of apothecia K+ purple-red. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; disc of apothecia with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor). Note: a Mediterranean to xeric subtropical species of base-rich siliceous rocks, often growing with species of Peltula, and starting the life-cycle on other crustose lichens; mostly Mediterranean, but also found, although very rarely, in dry-continental Alpine valleys. For further information see Wetmore (1996). See also note on C. furax. The epithet Callopisma conglomeratum Bagl. predates Lecanora peludella Nyl. (often spelled pellodella). The species is related to Pisutiella conversa (Vondrák in litt.).

choices.label: Apothecia with an orange proper exciple reacting K+ purple (containing anthraquinones)
Thallus not lichenicolous on aspicilioid species (rarely growing on various lichens when young). Ascospores c. 14-18 μm long
choices.name: Kuettlingeria xerica (Poelt & Vězda) I.V. Frolov, Vondrák & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, dark grey to almost black, epruinose, indistinctly areolate-cracked, rather thick (150-600 μm), the older parts blastidiate, the blastidia 100-350 μm in diam. Apothecia zeorine, subsessile, 0.4-0.8 mm across, with a flat to slightly convex, orange-brown disc, a thin, paler, orange-yellow proper margin, and a poorly developed, soon excluded, grey thalline margin. Thalline exciple 110-180 μm wide; proper exciple continuing in the lowermost part of the hypothecium, 70-110 μm wide laterally; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red, C-; hymenium colourless, 60-90 μm high; paraphyses mostly simple, 1-1.5 μm thick at base, the apical cells only slightly swollen, c. 2.5 μm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (11-)14-18(-19) x 5.5-9 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2.5-)3-6 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ faintly violet, C- or C+ violet, KC-, P-; disc of apothecia K+ red, C-. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; apothecia with fragilin (major), 7-chloremodin, emodic acid, parietin, and fragilin (minor or traces). The var. venostana Poelt has black apothecia devoid of anthraquinones. Note: on weathered basic siliceous rocks, both in the dry Mediterranean zone and in dry-continental Alpine valleys; perhaps more widespread in Eurasia; the var. venostana Poelt differs in the blackish apothecial disks.

choices.label: Thallus forming patches on the thalli of aspicilioid lichens. Ascospores c. 12-15 μm long
choices.name: Kuettlingeria furax (Egea & Llimona) I.V. Frolov, Vondrák & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose-subsquamulose, dark ash grey to lead-grey, dull, episubstratic, 135-175 μm thick, developing upon a black hypothallus on the thalli of aspicilioid lichens, forming 2-6 mm wide, often confluent patches with a sublobulate margin, which tend to die in central parts, the thalli becoming ring-like. Cortex 27-30 μm thick, the upper part violaceous grey, covered with a hyaline, 14-20 μm thick epinecral layer. Apothecia zeorine/lecanorine, 0.4-0.8 mm across, usually numerous, at first immersed and clearly provided with a grey thalline margin, then subsessile and with a rather thick, persistent, bright orange proper margin, the disc at first concave, then flat to slightly convex, orange to orange-brown. Proper exciple orange, corticate in outer part, K+ purple-red; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red, C+ purple, hymenium colourless, 80-90 μm high; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells slightly swollen, 2-3 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid to subglobose, often swollen at septum, (11.5-)12-15(-16) x 7-10 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 4-5.5 μm. Pycnidia dark, immersed in small thalline warts. Conidia broadly fusiform to weakly pyriform, 2-2.8 x 0.8-1.2 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ violet (section!), C- or C+ violet, KC-, P-; disc and proper margin of apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; disc and proper margin of apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones, mainly 7‐Cl‐emodin and fragilin. Note: on isolated boulders of base-rich or lime-containing siliceous rocks, more rarely on compact limestone and dolomite. This taxon was included in Caloplaca conglomerata by Nimis (1993: 162), but it clearly differs in the parasitic habit, in several morphological characters (see also Roux & coll. 2014), and in molecular data.

choices.label: Apothecia with a well-visible, yellow-orange proper margin. Apothecia C+ red, with at least traces of chlorinated anthraquinones. On more or less calciferous rocks
Apothecia with dark, or inapparent proper margin. Apothecia C-, without chlorinated anthraquinones. On siliceous rocks
On base-rich and lime-containing siliceous rocks above treeline. Not lichenicolous
choices.name: Kuettlingeria percrocata (Arnold) I.V. Frolov, Vondrák & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, areolate, whitish grey to dark grey, often with a bluish or brownish tinge, well-delimited, sometimes with a thin, dark grey prothallus, the areoles irregular, uneven, flat to convex, up to 3 mm wide. Cortex paraplectenchymatous, 15-35 µm thick, obscured by colourless crystals insoluble in K and soluble in N, K– or K+ faintly violet, N+ faintly violet; medulla with many crystals. Apothecia zeorine, often in groups, 0.4-1.5 mm across, round, angular or irregular in outline, at first semi-immersed but son becoming sessile, with a flat, brownish orange to brownish red disc contrasting with a paler, yellowish orange, thick, raised proper margin; thalline margin pale yellow, soon excluded and finally poorly visible. Thalline exciple ecorticate in lower part, or with an indistinct, up to 20 µm thick cortex; proper exciple of radiating hyphae; epithecium orange-brown K+ purple-red, C+ purple; hymenium colourless 90-120 µm high; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells up to 5(-6.5) µm wide; hypothecium colourless, with oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 14-18(-20) x 6-10(-12) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-6 µm (c. 1/3 of spore length). Pycnidia grey in upper part, the wall K+ violet. Conidia ellipsoid, 2.5-4 x 1.1.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ violet, C- or C+ violet, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment and chloroemodin; apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones ( 7‐Cl‐emodin and fragilin). Note: on base-rich and lime-containing siliceous rocks above treeline. The identity of Mediterranean samples (e.g. those from Sardinia) is dubious, and all records from Southern Italy reported by Nimis (1993: 180) are not accepted here.

choices.label: On limestone below the montane belt. Often lichenicolous on other crustose lichens
choices.name: Kuettlingeria areolata (Zahlbr.) I.V. Frolov, Vondrák & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, areolate, brown-grey to grey, 100-500 μm thick, forming irregular, up to 3 cm wide patches, often starting the life-cycle on the thalli of other crustose lichens. Areoles angular to rounded, flat to slightly convex, usually contiguous. Epinecral layer often present, to c. 10 μm thick; cortex of spherical, thin-walled cells, K+ faintly violet, N+ red in section; medulla well-developed only in thick thalli, loosely prosoplectenchymatous, non-amyloid. Apothecia frequent, zeorine, (0.3-)0.5-0.9(-1.3) mm across, with an initially orange, then dark orange brown to brown disc contrasting with a yellow to orange proper margin, and a grey thalline margin. Epithecium orange-brown, granular, K+ purple-red, C+ purple; hymenium colourless, c. 70–110 μm high, amyloid; paraphyses 2-2.5 μm thick in lower part, but gradually widening to 4-5 μm in upper part; hypothecium colourless, rarely with a few oil droplets, amyloid, with a subhypothecial algal layer. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid (8-)12-15(-17) x (5-)7-8(-9.5) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (4-)5-6(-7) μm. Pycnidia appearing as dark grey dots, the wall K+ violet. Conidia ellipsoid to tear-shaped. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P- (but sections of cortex K+ violet, N+ red); apothecial disc and proper margin K+ purple-red, C+ purple. Chemistry: cortex and top of pycnidia with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones (7‐Cl‐emodin, fragilin). Note: a mild-temperate, characteristic, but much misunderstood species found on the top of calcareous birds' perching boulders; in Northern Italy is mostly found at low altitudes, in Southern Italy it reaches the montane belt. This species was often synonymised with C. spalatensis Zahlbr., but according to Vondrák & al. (2013), the holotype of the latter species, contrary to what stated in the description, grows on siliceous rocks and has biatorine apothecia, being a poorly developed Blastenia.

choices.label: Thallus with 0.1-0.4 mm wide pustules and lobules. Proper margin of apothecia poorly evident
choices.name: Caloplaca thracopontica Vondrák & Šoun
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, grey to dark grey, usually covered in 0.1-0.4 mm wide pustules or lobules, often forming large patches, delimited by a lead-grey prothallus. Cortex conspicuous, grey in upper part and colourless in lower part, paraplectenchymatous, usually with a thick epinecral layer. Apothecia lecanorine, (0.3-)0.7-1(-1.5) mm across, with an orange to dark red, flat disc, and a raised, grey thalline margin. Proper exciple very thin, prosoplectenchymatous; epithecium orange, inspersed with granules of anthraquinones, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 60-110 µm high: paraphyses branched and anastomosing in upper part, 1.5-2.5 µm thick at mid-level, the apical cells to 5(-6.5) µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid to rarely narrowly ellipsoid, (10-)11-14(-15.5) x (3-)5-7(-10) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2.5-)5-7 µm, 1/3-1/2 of spore length. Pycnidia dark. Conidia bacilliform, 2.5-5.5 x 1-1.5 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and thalline margin of apothecia K+ faintly violet, C-, KC-, P- (reaction best visible on a thick section under the microscope); apothecial disc K+ purple-red. C-. Chemistry: thallus and thalline margin of apothecia with the Sedifolia-grey pigment: apothecial disc with parietin (major), plus low concentrations of teloschistin, fallacinal, parietinic acid and emodin. Note: on base-rich siliceous rocks, especially on basalt, not uncommon at least in parts of Tyrrhenian Italy. A lichen like this, belonging to the difficult C. cerina-complex, was often called Caloplaca chlorina by South European authors. The application of the epithet chlorina was very controversial until Wetmore (1996) solved the problem by examining the type material. Non-isidiate, fruiting specimens from Central and Southern Italy collected at low elevations on basic siliceous rocks, were provisionally called Caloplaca cerinoides (Anzi) Jatta by Nimis (1993: 159), but according to Vondrák (in litt.), who examined material of this species collected by Anzi, this is a probable synonym of C. atroflava. The specimens in TSB agree quite well with C. thracopontica, described from the Black Sea Region.

choices.label: Thallus rimose or areolate. Proper margin well-developed, dark-coloured

Apothecia up to 0.6 mm across, at first immersed in the thallus, then subsessile. Thalline margin of apothecia ecorticate in lower part. Thallus without a clear, shiny prothallus. Ascospores 7-11 x 5-7 µm, the thickening 2-5 µm
choices.name: Pisutiella conversa (Kremp.) S.Y. Kondr., Lőkös & Farkas
choices.description: Thallus crustose, mostly thinly episubstratic, continuous to usually rimose-areolate, pale to dark grey or grey-brown, sometimes almost black in sun-forms, usually without a distinct prothallus. Apothecia immersed to adnate, 0.2-0.6(-0.8) mm across, with an olive-yellow, dirty yellow-orange to dark brown, sometimes finally black, flat, epruinose disc and a persistent, dark grey to black margin. Thalline exciple filled by algae at least at the base, ecorticate throughout; proper exciple grey-brown in outer part, paraplectenchymatous, K+ faintly violet, N+ red; epithecium brownish orange or grey, the epipsamma K+ purple (K- in specimens without anthraquinones), the upper part of paraphyses K+ violet, C+ violet or K-, C-; hymenium colourless, 60-90 µm high; paraphyses slightly branched in upper part, the apical cells slightly swollen; hypothecium colourless to brownish. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 7-12 x 6-9 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 4–8.5 µm. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ violet, C- or C+ violet, KC-, P-; apothecial margin and epithecium K+ violet, C+ violet or K-, C-; epipsamma K+ purple or K- in specimens without anthraquinones. Chemistry: apothecia and sometimes thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment (blackened parts); apothecia with or without anthraquinones. Note: a mild-temperate to subtropical-montane lichen found on calciferous or basic siliceous rocks (especially basalt) in sunny sites with short periods of water seepage, often on colonies of cyanobacteria. According to Vondrák (in litt.) the species, which is related to Caloplaca conglomerata, is heterogeneous, and more species are involved, some of them fully lacking anthraquinones. An earlier record from Venezia Giulia (Nimis 1993: 162) has been excluded, being far from the Italian border.

choices.label: Apothecia up to 1 mm across, soon sessile. Thalline margin of apothecia corticate in lower part. Thallus with a clear, shiny prothallus. Ascospores 10-14 x 5-8 µm, the thickening 3-6 µm
On rocks in inland localities, mostly in upland areas
choices.name: Sanguineodiscus viridirufus (Ach.) I.V. Frolov & Vondrák
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, pale to dark grey, usually rimose-areolate, often delimited by an irregular, dark, somehow shiny prothallus. Apothecia zeorine/lecanorine, up to 1 mm across, initially immersed but soon sessile, with a brown-orange to brick red or finally blackish, flat, granular but epruinose disc, a persistent, dark grey, rather thick, sometimes verrucose cryptothalline margin and often a thin, dark parathecial ring. Thalline exciple eu-corticate in lower part, paraplectenchymatous; proper exciple well-developed, usually dark-pigmented in outer part, the pigmented parts K+ violet; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless; paraphyses mostly simple, with slightly swollen apical cells; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid, 10-15 x 5-8 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-6 μm, c. 1/3 of spore length. Pycnidia black. Conidia bacilliform, 5-6 x c. 1 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ faintly violet in section, C-, KC-, P-; apothecial disc K+ purple-red; proper exciple K+ violet. Chemistry: thallus and proper margin of apothecia with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; epithecium with unidentified anthraquinones. Note: this species, which is morphologically hardly distinguishable from the coastal-maritime S. aractinus, has however a different ecology, as it occur on inland siliceous rocks, mostly in upland areas (see Vondrák & Vitikainen 2008).

choices.label: On coastal rocks
choices.name: Sanguineodiscus aractinus (Fr.) I.V. Frolov & Vondrák
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, dark grey to almost black, continuous to usually rimose-areolate, often delimited by an irregular, dark, often somehow shiny prothallus. Apothecia zeorine/lecanorine, (0.2-)0.3-0.7(-1) mm across, initially immersed but soon sessile, with a brown-orange to brick red or finally blackish, flat, granular but epruinose disc, a persistent, dark grey, rather thick, sometimes verrucose thalline margin and often a thin, dark parathecial ring. Thalline exciple eu-corticate in lower part, paraplectenchymatous; proper exciple well-developed, usually dark-pigmented in outer part, the pigmented parts K+ faintly violet; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless; paraphyses mostly simple, with slightly swollen apical cells; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid, (10-)11-14(-15) x (5-)6-8 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-6 μm, c. 1/3 of spore length. Pycnidia black. Conidia bacilliform, 5-6 x c. 1 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ pale violet, C-, KC-, P-; apothecial disc K+ purple-red; proper exciple K+ violet. Chemistry: thallus and proper margin of apothecia with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; epithecium with unidentified anthraquinones. Note: a mild-temperate to subtropical lichen found on hard siliceous rocks near the coast. Earlier records from montane, inland areas were assigned to S. viridirufus (see note to that species).

choices.label: Proper margin. black, its cortex (section!) very dark green or very dark violet-brown to carbon black
Proper margin not black, its cortex not very dark
Ascospore septum 2-3(-4) μm long. Lichenicolous on several lichens in the Alpine belt
choices.name: Erichansenia epithallina (Lynge) S. Y. Kondr., Kärnefelt & A. Thell
choices.description: Thallus crustose, endosubstratic, forming paler patches on the thallus of the host lichens, or inapparent. Apothecia zeorine, 0.3-0.8(-1) mm across, often clustered in small groups, sessile, slightly to strongly constricted at base, with a flat to convex, dark orange to rusty red, finely granulose disc and a persistent to excluded, smooth to rough, often darkened margin. Proper exciple 20-120 μm wide, with many algal cells, the outer part corticate, almost black in mature apothecia, the inner part prosoplectenchymatous, hyaline, not amyloid; epithecium yellowish orange to ferruginous red, K+ purple-red, C+ purple in section; hymenium colourless, 50-60 μm high, not amyloid; paraphyses branched in upper part, the apical cells swollen, 3-4 μm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci (6-)8-spored, clavate, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid, (9-)11-13(-14) x 5.5-8 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2-4 μm (c. 1/2-1/3 of spore length). Thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple. Chemistry: apothecia with chlorinated and unchlorinated anthraquinones: 7-Cl-emodin (major), parietin (subdominant), emodin (minor), 7-Cl-emodinal (minor), 2 unknown compounds (minor). Note: a rather continental species found on sunny surfaces of siliceous rocks, e.g. on isolated boulders in grasslands, restricted to dry-continental Alpine valleys in Italy.

choices.label: Ascospore septum longer. Usually not lichenicolous
Proper margin of apothecia containing a grey pigment (Sedifolia-grey pigment), K+ violet, N+ red
Proper margin containing a grey-green pigment (Cinereorufa-green pigment), K-, N+ purple-red
On siliceous rocks
choices.name: Pisutiella conversa (Kremp.) S.Y. Kondr., Lőkös & Farkas
choices.description: Thallus crustose, mostly thinly episubstratic, continuous to usually rimose-areolate, pale to dark grey or grey-brown, sometimes almost black in sun-forms, usually without a distinct prothallus. Apothecia immersed to adnate, 0.2-0.6(-0.8) mm across, with an olive-yellow, dirty yellow-orange to dark brown, sometimes finally black, flat, epruinose disc and a persistent, dark grey to black margin. Thalline exciple filled by algae at least at the base, ecorticate throughout; proper exciple grey-brown in outer part, paraplectenchymatous, K+ faintly violet, N+ red; epithecium brownish orange or grey, the epipsamma K+ purple (K- in specimens without anthraquinones), the upper part of paraphyses K+ violet, C+ violet or K-, C-; hymenium colourless, 60-90 µm high; paraphyses slightly branched in upper part, the apical cells slightly swollen; hypothecium colourless to brownish. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 7-12 x 6-9 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 4–8.5 µm. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ violet, C- or C+ violet, KC-, P-; apothecial margin and epithecium K+ violet, C+ violet or K-, C-; epipsamma K+ purple or K- in specimens without anthraquinones. Chemistry: apothecia and sometimes thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment (blackened parts); apothecia with or without anthraquinones. Note: a mild-temperate to subtropical-montane lichen found on calciferous or basic siliceous rocks (especially basalt) in sunny sites with short periods of water seepage, often on colonies of cyanobacteria. According to Vondrák (in litt.) the species, which is related to Caloplaca conglomerata, is heterogeneous, and more species are involved, some of them fully lacking anthraquinones. An earlier record from Venezia Giulia (Nimis 1993: 162) has been excluded, being far from the Italian border.

choices.label: On calcareous rocks
choices.name: Kuettlingeria cretensis (Zahlbr.) I.V. Frolov & Vondrák
choices.description: Thallus crustose, endosubstratic and poorly evident, or thinly episubstratic and finely rimose-areolate, whitish, ochraceous, brownish or grey, rarely delimited by a black prothallus. Apothecia biatorine/zeorine, sessile and constricted at base, round, (0.1-)0.2-0.5(-0.6) mm across, with an orange, brownish orange to black, often orange-brown-pruinose, mostly flat to finally slightly convex disc, and an initially thick and smooth, finally often excluded, at first orange, then often blackening proper margin; on the same thallus the apothecia vary from completely orange to completely black, the blackening usually starting from the disc. Thalline exciple sometimes developed only at the base of the apothecia; proper exciple up to 100 µm thick, the outer part corticate, the inner part colourless; epithecium pale violet grey, with a granular, yellow-orange epipsamma reacting K+ purplish-red, C+ purple, the non-granular parts K+ violet; hymenium colourless, 60-120 µm high, not inspersed with oil droplets; paraphyses coherent, 1.5-2.5 µm thick at mid-level, the apical cells 2-4(-6) µm wide; hypothecium colourless, not inspersed with oil droplets, 60-120 µm high. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 10-17 x 4-9.5 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2-3.5(-5) µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: Thallus K- or K+ faintly violet in section, C-, KC-, P-. Apothecia K+ purple-red/violet, C+ purple. Chemistry: apothecia and sometimes thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment (blackened parts); apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones, mainly 7‐Cl‐emodin. Note: an (apparently) eastern Mediterranean species also known from southern France (Roux & coll. 2014), found on compact limestones, mostly coastal in Italy; probably more widespread in the Mediterranean Region than the few records would suggest.

choices.label: Hypothecium colourless, c. 80 μm high. Hymenium 60-85 μm high. Ascospores 5-7 μm wide
choices.name: Caloplaca conciliascens (Nyl.) Zahlbr.
choices.description: Thallus crustose, usually thinly episubstrati, continuous to areolate, greyish white, sometimes poorly evident. Apothecia lecideine, sessile, clustered, round to angular by mutual compression, 0.5-1 mm across, with a brownish red, flat to slightly convex disc, and a thin, black, persistent, slightly flexuose proper margin. Proper exciple without algae, blackish green in outer part, K-, N+ purple-red, colourless within; epithecium orange-brown, K+ violet-red; hymenium colourless, 60-85 μm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched in upper part, with slightly swollen apical cells; hypothecium colourless, inspersed with oil droplets, c. 80 μm high. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 10-14 x 5-7 μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-4(-5) μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-, N+ faintly violet. Chemistry: Cinereorufa-green pigment in thallus and apothecial margin; epithecium with non-chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a poorly known species, perhaps a synonym of Lendemeriella exsecuta, known from the locus classicus in Tyrol, Poland, a single locality in the French Maritime Alps (Roux & coll. 2014), and from dry-warm sites in central Sardinia and in Piemonte. The identification of the Sardinian collection is not completely certain (Nimis & Poelt 1987: 60). A detailed discussion of this species was provided by Wilk & Flakus (2006). The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: Hypothecium brownish, 50-125 μm high. Hymenium 65-135 μm high. Ascospores 5.5-8 μm wide
choices.name: Lendemeriella exsecuta (Nyl.) S. Y. Kondr.
choices.description: Thallus crustose, thinly episubstratic, continuous to rimose-areolate, grey, rarely dark grey or dirty white, the areoles 0.5-1 mm wide, sometimes constricted at base. Apothecia biatorine or lecideine, 0.2-0.7 mm across, sessile, not constricted at base, with a flat to convex disc of variable colour, from brownish yellow to orange-brown or finally entirely black (the yellow to orange pigment appearing as a pruina), and a persistent to finally excluded, black to olive, smooth proper margin. Proper exciple broad, prosoplectenchymatous, of anticlinally arranged, strongly coherent, 4-6 µm thick hyphae with thin lumina, the outer part blackish green to dark blue-green, K-, N+ purple-red; epithecium yellowish orange, with a granulose epipsamma, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 65-90(-135) μm high; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, the terminal cells swollen, 1.5-4 μm wide; hypothecium yellowish to brownish, inspersed with oil droplets, 50-125 μm high. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (10-)12-16.5 x (5.5-)6-7.5(-8) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-5(-7) μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K- or K+ purple-red, C-. Chemistry: Cinereorufa-green pigment in thallus and apothecial margin; apothecia with 7-chloroemodin, emodin, fallacinal, fragilin, parietin, parietinic acid, teloschistin and an unknown substance. Note: a mainly arctic-alpine, probably circumpolar lichen of basic siliceous rocks in humid, wind-protected situations above and near treeline; certainly much more widespread in the Alps.

choices.label: Apothecia rusty red, brownish red, dark orange-red, bright red to (at the end) blackish red
Apothecia yellow to orange
On calcareous rocks
On siliceous rocks
Apothecial disc epruinose
choices.name: Gyalolechia marmorata (Bagl.) Nimis & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, very variable, from endosubstratic and poorly evident to episubstratic and finely rimose-areolate, white to pale yellow, often delimited by a thin, black prothalline line. Apothecia biatorine, at first immersed, then sessile, rounded, 0.2-1.3 mm across, with a rusty red to dark orange-red, at first flat, then convex, epruinose disc, and a somewhat paler, smooth, at first well-visible, finally often excluded proper margin. Epithecium brownish orange, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 40-60(-80) µm high; paraphyses simple or forked in upper part, c. 1 µm thick at base, the apical cells (2-)3-4.5 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (9-)10-13(-14) x (3-)5-6(-10) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) up to 5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ faintly purple-red; C-, KC-, P-; Apothecia K+ purple-red. Chemistry: thallus without lichen substances or with low amounts of fragilin; apothecia with parietin and emodin (major), and citreorosein, emodinal, fallacinal and parietinic acid (minor). Note: a Mediterranean species found on compact limestone, locally very abundant in coastal situations, rare far from the coast (Arup & al.2023).

choices.label: Apothecial disc coarsely orange-red-pruinose
choices.name: Flavoplaca tavaresiana (Nav.-Ros. & Cl. Roux) Arup, Frödén & Søchting
choices.description: Thallus crustose, endosubstratic and poorly evident or thinly episubstratic and then whitish to whitish-grey, continuous to rimose-areolate, without a distinct prothallus. Apothecia zeorine, bright orange-red, (0.1-)0.2-0.8(-1) mm across, usually numerous, rounded or deformed by mutual compression, at first immersed and urceolate, then adnate to sessile and constricted at base, with a concave to finally slightly convex, coarsely orange-red-pruinose disc, and an initially thick, smooth, epruinose, finally reduced but usually persistent proper margin; a whitish thalline rim is sometimes visible at the base of the apothecium. Thalline exciple poorly developed, but rich in algal cells; proper exciple 40-100 µm wide, prosoplectenchymatous, thinly corticate and orange-red in outer part, the medulla colourless, of radiating hyphae; epithecium yellow-red, 8-10 µm high, K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless, 60-80 µm high; paraphyses simple or forked, 1.5-2 µm thick at mid-level, the apical cells 4.5-7 µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (9-)10-13(-14.5) x (4-)5-7(-8) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (3.5-)4-6(-7) µm (less than half of spore length). Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red. Chemistry: apothecia (rarely also thallus) with parietin (major), fallacinal, emodin, teloschistin and parietinic acid (minor), corresponding with chemosyndrome A of Søchting (1997). Note: a Mediterranean, recently-described species found on soft calcareous substrata (incl. mortar) near the coast; locally very abundant, to be looked for throughout coastal Mediterranean Italy. The sample from Tuscany was collected at Porto Ercole, on coastal calcareous rocks.

choices.label: Lichenicolous on Miriquidica nigroleprosa
choices.name: Caloplaca magni-filii Poelt
choices.description: Thallus crustose, poorly evident, completely immersed in the thalli of Miriquidica nigroleprosa. Apothecia zeorine, sparse, 0.2-0.5 mm across, with a rust-red to orange-red, flat to convex, rough disc, and a slightly raised, sometimes greyish-orange, finally often excluded proper margin. Proper exciple relatively thick, with algae in lower part, I+ distinctly blue; epithecium brownish orange, K+ red, C+ purple (section!); hymenium colourless, 50-70 µm high; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched, the apical cells only slightly swollen; hypothecium colourless. Asci (6-)8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, broadly ellipsoid, 10-12 x 5-6 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 2.5-4 µm thick, or subglobose, c. 10 µm wide, the equatorial thickening 2.5-3.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple (the last reaction best observed in thick sections under the microscope). Chemistry: apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: exclusively parasite on thalli of the silicicolous Miriquidica nigroleprosa, usually from the high montane to the lower alpine belt; widespread in the European parts of the Holarctic, including the Alps, but rare; not reported from Italy, to be looked for in the Alps. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: Not on Miriquidica nigroleprosa
Proper margin of apothecia thick, paler than the brownish orange to brownish red disc
choices.name: Kuettlingeria percrocata (Arnold) I.V. Frolov, Vondrák & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, areolate, whitish grey to dark grey, often with a bluish or brownish tinge, well-delimited, sometimes with a thin, dark grey prothallus, the areoles irregular, uneven, flat to convex, up to 3 mm wide. Cortex paraplectenchymatous, 15-35 µm thick, obscured by colourless crystals insoluble in K and soluble in N, K– or K+ faintly violet, N+ faintly violet; medulla with many crystals. Apothecia zeorine, often in groups, 0.4-1.5 mm across, round, angular or irregular in outline, at first semi-immersed but son becoming sessile, with a flat, brownish orange to brownish red disc contrasting with a paler, yellowish orange, thick, raised proper margin; thalline margin pale yellow, soon excluded and finally poorly visible. Thalline exciple ecorticate in lower part, or with an indistinct, up to 20 µm thick cortex; proper exciple of radiating hyphae; epithecium orange-brown K+ purple-red, C+ purple; hymenium colourless 90-120 µm high; paraphyses sparingly branched in upper part, the apical cells up to 5(-6.5) µm wide; hypothecium colourless, with oil droplets. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 14-18(-20) x 6-10(-12) µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3-6 µm (c. 1/3 of spore length). Pycnidia grey in upper part, the wall K+ violet. Conidia ellipsoid, 2.5-4 x 1.1.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ violet, C- or C+ violet, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment and chloroemodin; apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones ( 7‐Cl‐emodin and fragilin). Note: on base-rich and lime-containing siliceous rocks above treeline. The identity of Mediterranean samples (e.g. those from Sardinia) is dubious, and all records from Southern Italy reported by Nimis (1993: 180) are not accepted here.

choices.label: Proper margin more or less concolorous with disc
Apothecia 0.2-0.4 mm across, dark rust-red, finally blackish, often with a well-developed thalline margin when young. Ascospores 10-13 x 4-5(-6) μm
choices.name: Rufoplaca scotoplaca (Nyl.) Arup, Søchting & Frödén
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, thin, continuous to rimose-areolate, ash-grey to dark grey-brown, often delimited by a dark prothallus, the areoles 0.2-0.4 mm wide, 0.1-0.2 mm thick, irregular, flat to uneven, separated by very thin, often indistinct cracks. Apothecia appressed to sessile, circular to angular by mutual compression, 0.2-0.4(-0.5) mm across, with a flat to slightly convex, bright to dark rust-red, finally rarely blackening disc, a thin, mostly persistent, at first paler, then concolorous (or blackened), rarely excluded proper margin, and a grey thalline margin which is evident at least in young apothecia. Proper exciple brownish yellow in outer part, colourless within; epithecium brownish yellow, inspersed with orange-yellow crystals of anthraquinones reacting K+ purple-red; hymenium colourless or yellowish in upper part, 60-70 μm high, amyloid; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched in upper part, c. 1.7 μm thick at base, the apical cells swollen, 4-5 μm wide; hypothecium 20-50 μm high, colourless to greyish, I+ dark blue. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, narrowly ellipsoid, 10-13 x (3-)4-6(-8) μm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) (2-)3-4(-5) μm, 1/4-1/3 of spore length. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K- or K+ weakly violet in section, C- or C+ violet (reaction visible only in sections) KC-, P-; disc of apothecia K+ purple-red, C-. Chemistry: thallus with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; disc of apothecia with non-chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: at least in Southern Europe this lichen of basic, hard siliceous rocks has been much misunderstood; several earlier Italian records, especially those from outside the Alps, need confirmation, as well as those from Sardinia (see Nimis & Poelt 1987: 74).

choices.label: Apothecia 0.3-1.5 mm across, brown to bright rust-red, sometimes finally lead-grey, rarely blackening. Ascospores larger
Both apothecial disc and margin C+ purple (in section), with chlorinated anthraquinones. Melanisation by the Sedifolia‐grey pigment (K+ violet, N+ violet in section)
At least the apothecial disc C-, without chlorinated anthraquinones. Melanisation by the Cinereorufa‐green pigment (K-, N+ violet in section)
Apothecia orange-brown. Ascospores 16-27(-30) x 9-13 μm
choices.name: Caloplaca sbarbaronis B. de Lesd.
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, dirty white to ochre-white, relatively thick, granulose-subsquamulose, consisting of small, contiguous (rarely scattered), angular areoles separated by thin fissures. Apothecia 0.3-0.5 mm across, orange-brown, reddish brown to finally almost black, sessile, with an initially flat then convex (sometimes finally almost hemispherical) disc and a very thin, concolorous, soon excluded proper margin. Epithecium yellowish, granulose, K+ purple-red, C+ purple; hymenium colourless, 130-150 μm high; paraphyses rather lax, mostly simple, capitate; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 16-27(-30) x 9-13 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple. Chemistry: thallus without lichen substances; apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones. Note: a poorly-known, apparently coastal, silicicolous species. Claude Roux (in litt.) has examined the type material in MARSS: the brownish apothecia react C+ red (chlorinated anthraquinones), and the ascospores measure 16-27(-30) x 9-13 µm. The species does not belong to Caloplaca s.str.

choices.label: Apothecia orange-red to rusty red. Ascospores 13-18 x 7-10 µm
Thallus usually <150 µm thick, with thin, to 0.6 mm wide marginal areoles. Apothecia with traces of citreorosein and emodinal
choices.name: Kuettlingeria neotaurica (Vondrák, Khodos., Arup & Søchting) I.V. Frolov, Vondrák & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, usually <150 µm thick, dark grey to brown-black, rarely white-pruinose, continuous to rimose or indistinctly areolate, delimited by a dark grey prothallus. Apothecia biatorine, up to 0.7 mm across, with an orange-red disc (grey in variants without anthraquinones), and a usually paler proper margin. Proper exciple c. 100-130 µm thick, prosoplectenchymatous; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red, C+ purple; hymenium colourless, 90-110 µm high; paraphyses branched and anastomosing, the apical cells to 5(-6) µm wide; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, 14-17 x 7.5-10.5 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 4-7.5 µm. Pycnidia common, dark, the wall darker and K+ violet around the ostiole. Conidia narrowly ellipsoid, 2.5-3.5 x 1-1.5 µm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus and pycnidial walls K+ fleeting violet, C-, KC-, P-, N+ purple; apothecia K+ and C+ purple-red (reactions best seen in thick sections under the microscope). Chemistry: thallus and pycnidial walls with the Sedifolia-grey pigment; apothecia with chlorinated anthraquinones, 7-Cl-emodin major, citreorosein and emodinal in traces(chemosyndrome C2 sensu Søchting 2001). Note: a recently-described, mainly coastal species of siliceous rocks, related to K. fuscoatroides. The sample from Liguria was collected on coastal siliceous cliffs near Levanto. The identity of the samples collected by Vondrák in upland areas of Calabria and Sicily awaits confirmation based on molecular data.

choices.label: Thallus 100-350 µm thick, with subsquamulose, to 2 mm wide marginal areoles. Apothecia without citreorosein and emodinal
choices.name: Kuettlingeria fuscoatroides (J. Steiner) I.V. Frolov, Vondrák & Arup
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, dark grey to almost black, rimose or usually areolate, 0.1-0.35 mm thick, the marginal areoles larger and almost subsquamulose, sometimes delimited by a black prothallus. Cortex thin, paraplectenchymatous, the upper part grey, K+ faintly violet in section; medulla poorly developed. Apothecia zeorine, rusty red but tending to turn lead-grey to blackish, 0.3-1.5 mm across, with a flat to finally convex disc and a raised, persistent, concolorous or paler proper margin. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous; epithecium orange-brown, K+ purple-red, C+ purple; hymenium and hypothecium colourless; paraphyses slightly swollen at apices. Asci 8-spored, cylindrical-clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, 13-18 x 7-10 µm. the equatorial thickening (“septum”) 3.5-8 µm. Pycnidia dark grey to black, the wall K+ violet. Conidia bacilliform. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K+ faintly violet in section, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ purple-red, C+ purple. Chemistry: Sedifolia-grey pigment in thallus and pycnidia; chlorinated anthraquinones in both disc and margin of apothecia (always with fragilin and without citreorosein and emodinal). Note: a widespread Mediterranean lichen found on base-rich siliceous rocks wetted by rain. The sample from Calabria was collected at Melito di Porto Salvo, Riaci Capo, on sandstone, that from Liguria near Levanto, Vernazza.

choices.label: Black prothallus conspicuous. Apothecia often blackened at margins. Pycnidia black or red
Black prothallus lacking or thin. Apothecia rarely blackened at margins. Pycnidia always red
Species of upland areas in the Mediterranean mountains
choices.name: Blastenia gennargentuae Vondrák
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, grey, up to 150 μm thick when young, but old thalli with up to 800 μm thick, convex to bullate areoles, often with a black hypothallus visible among the areoles and forming a black layer in the medulla, delimited by a conspicuous, black prothalline line. Apothecia biatorine/zeorine, 0.7-1 mm across, with a red disc and an often blackened proper margin. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, the outer part often blackened, C+ purple; epithecium orange-brown, K+ red, C-; hymenium colourless, not inspersed with oil droplets; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched and anastomosing, 1.5-3 μm thick in lower part, the apical cells usually wider; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, functionally unitunicate, apically thickened with a broad internal beak, the inner part of apex and external cap I+ blue, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid, (10-)12-14(-15) x 6-7 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) c. 5 µm. Pycnidia dark grey. Conidia bacilliform, rarely narrowly ellipsoid, 3-5 x 1-1.5 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-, N+ violet in section; apothecia K+ red, the exciple C+ purple. Chemistry: non-chlorinated anthraquinones in apothecial disc (C-), chlorinated anthraquinones in exciple (C+ purple); thallus without anthraquinones; the Cinereorufa-green pigment (K-, N+ violet in section) forms black patches in thallus, apothecia and pycnidia and often expands into medullary tissue, forming a black hypothallus. For further details see Vondrák & al. (2020). Note: A recently-described species of siliceous rocks in the Mediterranean mountains (Gennargentu, Aspromonte). The records from Calabria (Aspromonte) were cited by Nimis (1993: 167) under B. festivella.

choices.label: Species of Mediterranean areas, mostly near the coast or in the lowlands
choices.name: Blastenia festivella (Nyl.) Vondrák
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, grey, up to 150 μm thick when young (old thalli with convex to bullate areoles may be thicker, up to 800 μm), delimited by a conspicuous black prothallus. Apothecia biatorine/zeorine, rusty red, 0.7-1.1 mm across, with a flat to slightly convex disc and a raised, sometimes blackened proper margin. Proper exciple prosoplectenchymatous, C+ fleeting purple; epithecium orange-brown, granular, K+ red, C-; hymenium colourless, not inspersed with oil droplets; paraphyses simple or sparingly branched and anastomosing, 1.5-3 μm thick in lower part, the apical cells usually wider; hypothecium colourless. Asci 8-spored, clavate, Teloschistes-type. Ascospores 2-celled, polarilocular, hyaline, ellipsoid (11-13(-17.5) x 6-9 µm, the equatorial thickening (“septum”) c. 6 µm. Pycnidia dark grey, with the Cinereorufa-green pigment, rarely with anthraquinones. Conidia bacilliform, rarely narrowly ellipsoid, 3-5 x 1-1.5 μm. Photobiont chlorococcoid. Spot tests: thallus K-, C-, KC-, P-; apothecia K+ red. Chemistry: non-chlorinated anthraquinones in apothecial disc (C-), chlorinated anthraquinones in exciple (C+ purple); Cinereorufa-green pigment in prothallus, pycnidial walls and sometimes apothecial margin (K-, N+ violet in section). For further details see Vondrák & al. (2020). Note: a Mediterranean-Macaronesian lichen found on hard siliceous rocks, from granite to basalt, usually (but not always) not far from the coast, exclusively Tyrrhenian in Italy. The species could be identical with Caloplaca limitosa, in which case the epithet limitosa would have priority (Vondrák & al. 2020). Earlier records from Calabria (Nimis 1993: 167) refer to B. gennargentuae.

choices.label: Species of the Alpine belt (Alps, N Apennines). Hymenium not inspersed with oil droplets
choices.name: Blastenia psychrophila Halıcı & Vondrák
choices.description: Thallus crustose, episubstratic, grey (exceptionally with a yellowish tinge), partly >100 μm thick, rarely with rough, isidia-like outgrowths. Apothecia biatorine/zeorine, rust-red, 0.7-1.1 mm across.
